# @zakkster/lite-o1

Version: 1.9.0
License: MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev <shinikchiev@yahoo.com>
Runtime dependencies: none. ESM only. ASCII-only source. sideEffects: false.
Node: >= 18.

## What it is

A tree-shakeable, zero-GC family of O(1) data structures that WITNESSES its
constant instead of asserting it. The complexity class is the product: every hot
op is O(1) worst-case (or O(1)-amortized where stated) and allocates zero bytes
after construction, and a shipped witness harness demonstrates the flat
throughput curve against a built-in foil.

v1.9.0 ships nineteen members: SparseSet, RingDeque, UnionFind, MonoDeque, MinStack,
RandomSet, FreqO1, BucketQueue, TimerWheel, HierarchicalTimerWheel, RingLog, CuckooMap,
SparseTable, BitSet, AliasTable, CoarseTimerWheel, WindowFold, RankSelect, and EliasFano. They share no
mutable module state, so a bundler that imports one drops the others (tree-shakeable). 1.9.0 adds
EliasFano (the nineteenth member; 1.8.0 added RankSelect, 1.7.0 added WindowFold, 1.6.0 added
CoarseTimerWheel, 1.5.0 added AliasTable, 1.4.0 added BitSet, 1.3.0 added SparseTable, 1.2.0 added
CuckooMap, 1.1.0 added RingLog).

## Exports (from the single main file O1.js)

- `SparseSet` -- class. A zero-GC O(1) integer set over [0, universe).
- `RingDeque` -- class. A zero-GC O(1) fixed-capacity numeric double-ended queue.
- `UnionFind` -- class. A zero-GC near-O(1) amortized disjoint-set forest.
- `MonoDeque` -- class. A zero-GC O(1)-amortized monotonic deque for
  sliding-window min / max.
- `MinStack` -- class. A zero-GC WORST-CASE O(1) fixed-capacity numeric stack with
  a running min / max.
- `RandomSet` -- class. A zero-GC O(1) integer set (SparseSet substrate) with
  WORST-CASE O(1) uniform sample() + removeRandom().
- `FreqO1` -- class. A zero-GC WORST-CASE O(1) LFU frequency structure with
  add() / increment() / peekMin() / popMin() over a private bucket forest.
- `BucketQueue` -- class. A zero-GC AMORTIZED O(1) monotone integer priority queue
  ("Dial") with insert() / decreaseKey() / extractMin() / peekMin() over private key
  columns + a static per-priority bucket array.
- `TimerWheel` -- class. A zero-GC WORST-CASE O(1) bounded "simple" timing wheel
  (Varghese-Lauck) with schedule() / cancel() / drainDue() / advance() over private id
  columns + a static per-slot FIFO ring.
- `HierarchicalTimerWheel` -- class. A zero-GC AMORTIZED O(1) CASCADING multi-level
  timing wheel (four levels in the Linux tvec shape 1x256 + 3x64, delay range 2^26)
  with schedule() / cancel() / drainDue() / advance() over private id columns + a
  Float64 expiry column + static per-list FIFO rings; coarse timers cascade down to
  finer levels by INDEX as the clock advances.
- `RingLog` -- class. A zero-GC WORST-CASE O(1) fixed-capacity LOSSY overwrite-oldest
  ring log ("keep the last N") over ONE Float64Array. push() never blocks / never
  throws on full -- it OVERWRITES the oldest entry and RETURNS it (undefined until
  full). Read-only snapshot surface get() / oldest() / newest() / forEach() / iterate;
  NO drain (inverts RingDeque's fail-closed policy).
- `CuckooMap` -- class. A zero-GC bounded-probe exact map from GENERAL INTEGER keys
  (|k| <= 2^53) to numbers, via bucketized cuckoo hashing (2 tables x 4 slots). get() /
  has() / delete() are WORST-CASE O(1) (<= 8 slot reads); set() is AMORTIZED O(1) (an
  eviction chain + a rare in-place O(capacity) re-seed -- the max-single-op line). Fixed
  capacity, fail closed under a 0.90 load ceiling. 0 is a legal key (occupancy byte is the
  only emptiness signal). O(capacity) space over a sparse / large integer key domain.
- `SparseTable` -- class. A zero-GC WORST-CASE O(1)-QUERY STATIC range-minimum / range-maximum
  table (the idempotent-operation sparse table / "StaticRMQ") -- the suite's FIRST static
  build-once/immutable member. query(l, r) is true worst-case O(1) (a floor-log2 via clz32 + two
  table reads + one compare, independent of the range width); the O(n log n) BUILD and O(n log n)
  table SPACE are a DISCLOSED co-headline paid once at construction. kind ('min' | 'max') frozen;
  the source is COPIED into an internal Float64Array (immutable). Build-once, query-only (NO
  mutators, NO clear); fail closed at construction, queries never throw.
- `BitSet` -- class. A zero-GC, FIXED-capacity, WORST-CASE O(1) multi-word dense bitset over MANY
  Uint32 words (N >> 32) -- the canonical membership / flag structure for visited sets, dirty
  masks, replay windows, permission bitmaps at scale. test() / set() / unset() / toggle() are
  worst-case O(1) per-bit (one word load + one mask op); firstSet() / nextSet() are worst-case
  O(1) via a 3-LEVEL popcount summary (fan-out 32; a fixed <= 32-word top scan + a 3-hop
  clz32/ctz32 descent, never an O(words) scan). Bulk and()/or()/xor()/andNot() (in place,
  capacity-match-or-throw) + popcount()/setAll()/clear()/forEach()/iterate are O(words) -- a
  DISCLOSED co-headline, NOT the per-bit claim, and still 0 B/op. NON-OVERLAP: BitSet is the
  MULTI-WORD structure; @zakkster/lite-fastbit32 stays the single 32-flag word and
  @zakkster/lite-scheduler's FastBitScheduler the bit-bucket scheduler (design-parity only, ZERO
  runtime dep). Fixed capacity, fail closed at construction; test/firstSet/nextSet never throw.
- `AliasTable` -- class. A zero-GC, WORST-CASE O(1) STATIC Vose weighted sampler -- the suite's
  SECOND static build-once / immutable member and the WEIGHTED complement to RandomSet's uniform
  draw. Build a table from a fixed weight vector ONCE (an O(n) precompute), then sample() draws an
  outcome index in [0, n) by WEIGHT in worst-case O(1) (two LCG advances + one Float64 compare +
  one Uint32 read, independent of n and of the weight distribution). Loot tables, weighted
  load-balancing, Monte-Carlo, procedural generation. The O(n) BUILD and 2n Float64/Uint32 SPACE
  are a DISCLOSED co-headline paid once at construction (the SparseTable precedent). weightOf(i)
  reads the original input weight; the caller's weights are COPIED in (immutable); a per-instance
  seeded LCG makes it reproducible (clear() resets to the seed). Build-once, sample-only (NO
  mutators / reweight); fail closed at construction, sample()/weightOf() never throw.
- `CoarseTimerWheel` -- class. A zero-GC, WORST-CASE O(1), NON-CASCADING, near-unbounded
  timing wheel with an APPROXIMATE (bounded, one-sided-LATE) fire time -- the Linux-4.8
  coarse-bucket model (9 levels x 64 buckets, per-level clock shift 3n, granularity 8^n).
  schedule() / cancel() / drainDue() / advance() are worst-case O(1) with NO cascade and NO
  max-single-op line (it touches <= 9 levels/buckets, independent of live count and delay
  magnitude), via a per-bucket occupancy BITMAP (18 x Uint32) find-first-set. A far-future
  timer sits in a coarse bucket and fires IN PLACE. The trade is PRECISION for range: a timer
  fires LATE by at most gran(level) - 1 (<= 12.5% relative, ONE-SIDED never early; L0 EXACT) --
  the disclosed co-headline. Near-unbounded delay in [0, 62 x 2^24) (~0.97 x 2^30; the Linux
  phase margin below the full 2^30 span). peekNext() (next due tick, NOHZ) + fireTimeOf(id)
  (the rounded fire tick) are O(1) queries. For EXACT far-future deadlines use a min-heap
  (@zakkster/lite-logn). NO payload storage. Fail closed on schedule/advance; queries never throw.
- `WindowFold` -- class. A zero-GC, WORST-CASE O(1) GENERAL FIFO sliding-window aggregator
  (DABA-Lite -- the De-Amortized Banker's Aggregator, IBM Research) over TWO Float64Array columns.
  push(v) / evict() / query() are each worst-case O(1) (<= 2 combines, NO window-size branch, NO
  closure, 0 B/op) for ANY of FOUR frozen associative operators (a monoid): SUM (identity 0), MIN
  (+Infinity), MAX (-Infinity), PRODUCT (1). The operator is frozen at construction (the MonoDeque
  frozen-kind pattern -- a ctor-cached int drives a switch-free combine). query() on an EMPTY window
  returns the operator IDENTITY (never undefined). The classic two-stacks would flip (reverse the
  back into a fresh front) with an O(W) evict spike; DABA-Lite DE-AMORTIZES that flip one step per
  op, so there is NO max-single-op line (the worst-case cohort). It is the GENERAL member and does
  min/max worst-case; MonoDeque stays the lower-constant amortized min/max specialist. Caller-driven
  primitive (count/time/event windows). Fixed capacity (rounds up to a power of two), fail closed;
  query() never throws. The bitwise trio (AND/OR/XOR) is DEFERRED to a future int32-lane sibling
  WindowFoldInt32. For arbitrary-index / out-of-order range queries use @zakkster/lite-logn Fenwick.
- `RankSelect` -- class. A zero-GC, WORST-CASE O(1) STATIC succinct rank/select bitvector index
  over a frozen bit pattern (cs-poppy: 512-bit basic blocks + a select sampling layer). Built from a
  RAW WORD ARRAY (Array | numeric TypedArray) + an explicit nbits, COPIED into a private Uint32Array
  (immutable, NOT a BitSet instance -- zero coupling). rank1(i) / rank0(i) count set / clear bits in
  [0, i); select1(k) / select0(k) return the position of the k-th set / clear bit (0-indexed);
  access(i) is the bit at i. All are worst-case O(1), 0 B/op (a fixed directory lookup + a bounded
  <= 16-word block scan + a bounded in-word step). The O(n) build + the ~3.2% index space are a
  DISCLOSED co-headline (the SparseTable / AliasTable static-member contract), EXCLUDED from the
  per-op claim, so there is NO max-single-op line. size (popcount) + length (nbits) + indexBytes are
  O(1) getters; forEach(fn) is the O(n) scan exception. Fail closed on nbits (typeof-safe, before any
  alloc); queries never throw (bad i -> rank 0 / access undefined; bad/overflow k -> select -1).
  @zakkster/lite-loglogn re-adopts it as its rank/select substrate.
- `EliasFano` -- class. A zero-GC, succinct STATIC encoding of a monotone non-decreasing integer
  sequence (quasi-succinct, ~2 + ceil(log2(U/n)) bits/element), built on a COMPOSED RankSelect over
  the upper bits. Build once from a SORTED numeric Array | TypedArray (U inferred as max + 1; the
  values are ENCODED, not referenced). access(i) is the i-th value in WORST-CASE O(1) (one select1 +
  one packed low read); nextGEQ(x) is the smallest value >= x and is DATA-DEPENDENT -- O(1) TYPICAL
  on well-distributed keys, O(log n) WORST-CASE on clustered keys (an in-bucket binary search after an
  O(1) select0 seek), a third honesty category (neither clean "expected O(1)" nor worst-case O(1)).
  The O(n) build + the succinct space are a DISCLOSED co-headline; access joins the worst-case cohort
  (NO max-single-op line). length / size (= n) / universe (= U) / bitsPerElement / sizeBytes are O(1)
  getters; forEach(fn) is the O(n) decode exception. Build-once, query-only: NO mutators. Fail closed
  on an unsorted / out-of-range source (typeof-first, before any alloc); queries never throw (bad i ->
  access undefined; x > max or bad x -> nextGEQ -1). Elias-Fano's sub-log successor is a DEFERRED
  follow-on's job (@zakkster/lite-loglogn); for arbitrary-index range queries use @zakkster/lite-logn.
- `VERSION` -- string, '1.9.0'.

## SparseSet

    new SparseSet(universe, capacity = universe)

- universe: exclusive key ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Sizes the sparse array.
- capacity: max live members; integer in [1, universe], default universe. Sizes
  the dense array.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / out-of-range arg.

Hot surface (all O(1) worst-case, zero allocation):

- add(k) -> this        Insert; idempotent. Throws [lite-o1] on a bad key
                        (not an integer in [0, universe): -1, 1.5, NaN, null,
                        k === universe) or when a NEW key exceeds capacity.
                        Re-adding a present key when full is a no-op.
- has(k) -> boolean     Membership. A bad key is ABSENT, never a throw. null is
                        not zero: has(null) is false even when 0 is a member.
- delete(k) -> boolean  Remove by swapping the last dense entry into the hole and
                        fixing its back-pointer. true iff k was present. Never throws.
- clear() -> void       Empty in O(1): resets the live count, zeroes NO store.
                        Stale sparse pointers fail the has() cross-check.
- forEach(fn) -> void   Iterate present keys in insertion order, alloc-free.
                        fn is (key, set).
- [Symbol.iterator]()   Iterate present keys in insertion order.
- size (getter)         Live member count.
- capacity (getter)     Max live members as constructed.

Membership invariant (the whole trick):

    has(k) == sparse[k] < n && dense[sparse[k]] === k

The cross-check rejects stale sparse pointers, which is why clear() can be O(1)
and never zero a store.

## RingDeque

    new RingDeque(capacity)

- capacity: requested max elements; integer in [1, 2^31]. ROUNDS UP to the next
  power of two (>= requested); the capacity getter reports the rounded value.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / out-of-range /
  non-number arg (typeof-guarded before any coercion; message via String(x)).
- Substrate: ONE Float64Array (numeric values only), head + count representation.
  The physical slot for logical offset i from the front is store[(head + i) & MASK],
  MASK = capacity - 1; wrap is a single & (power-of-two modulo), no branch.

Hot surface (all O(1) worst-case, zero allocation):

- pushFront(v) -> this   Push v onto the front. Throws [lite-o1] when FULL (a
                         byte-identical no-op) or on a non-clean value.
- pushBack(v) -> this    Push v onto the back. Same fail-closed policy.
- popFront() -> number|undefined  Remove+return the front; undefined on empty (never throws).
- popBack()  -> number|undefined  Remove+return the back; undefined on empty (never throws).
- peekFront() -> number|undefined Front without removing; undefined on empty.
- peekBack()  -> number|undefined Back without removing; undefined on empty.
- clear() -> void        Empty in O(1): resets head + count, touches NO store
                         (numbers retain no references, so nothing to zero).
- forEach(fn) -> void    Iterate live elements front->back, alloc-free.
                         fn is (value, index, deque).
- [Symbol.iterator]()    Iterate live elements front->back.
- size (getter)          Live element count.
- capacity (getter)      Max elements (power-of-two, rounded up from requested).

Value contract (LOCKED): a pushed value must be typeof 'number' AND not NaN.
Rejected (throws [lite-o1]): null, undefined, string, Symbol, BigInt, object, NaN.
Accepted: any finite number, and +Infinity / -Infinity (typeof number, not NaN).
The typeof guard runs FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches arithmetic.

## UnionFind

    new UnionFind(n)

- n: fixed element count; integer in [1, 2^32-1]. Elements are [0, n).
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / out-of-range arg
  (Number.isInteger never coerces; message via String(n), Symbol/BigInt-safe).
- Substrate: TWO flat Uint32Array columns -- parent[i] (i's parent; i itself iff
  root) and size[root] (elements in that tree). Path halving on find + union by
  size bound any single op at O(alpha(n)) amortized (inverse Ackermann, <= ~4).

Hot surface (all O(1)-AMORTIZED, zero allocation):

- find(x) -> number      Root of x's component. Path halving flattens the walk in
                         place (no recursion, no stack array). Throws [lite-o1] on
                         a bad element (typeof-guarded before the coercing >>>).
- union(a,b) -> boolean  Merge a and b. true iff a real merge happened (they were
                         separate); false if already joined. Union by size. Guards
                         both endpoints. count-- exactly once per true merge.
- connected(a,b) -> boolean  find(a) === find(b). Both guarded via find.
- componentSize(x) -> number size[find(x)]. Guarded via find.
- count (getter)         Live component count. O(1), maintained (never scanned).
- capacity (getter)      Fixed element universe n. (No `size` getter -- it would
                         collide with the live-count meaning size has elsewhere.)
- reset() -> void        O(n) HONEST EXCEPTION: re-singleton every element
                         (parent[i]=i, size[i]=1, count=n). A single bulk pass over
                         the existing arrays -- allocates NOTHING, but is O(n), NOT
                         a zero-alloc-per-op hot path. Named reset(), not clear().
- forEachRoots(fn) -> void  O(n) FULL SCAN, alloc-free: fn(root, uf) per current
                         root. Documented exception, EXCLUDED from the
                         zero-alloc-per-op claims. fn is hoisted for zero alloc.
- roots() -> generator   O(n) scan; ALLOCATES a generator + {value,done} per step
                         by protocol (like [Symbol.iterator]) -- OUT of zero-alloc
                         claims. Use forEachRoots for the alloc-free scan.

Amortized honesty: a single find is NOT worst-case O(1) -- an adversarial
pre-halving chain is O(depth). The guarantee is AMORTIZED alpha(n); the witness
reports amortized throughput staying flat while a no-compression / no-union-by-size
foil (a degenerate chain) collapses.

## MonoDeque

    new MonoDeque(capacity, kind)

- capacity: max simultaneously-live entries; integer in [1, 2^31]. ROUNDS UP to
  the next power of two; the capacity getter reports the rounded value.
- kind: 'min' or 'max', FROZEN at construction (one monotone invariant per
  instance). Validated fail-closed (anything else throws [lite-o1]).
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad capacity (non-integer /
  out-of-range / non-number, typeof-guarded before coercion) or a bad kind.
- Substrate: TWO parallel Float64Arrays (value + monotonic seq) inside a
  head + count power-of-two ring; wrap is a single & (capacity - 1). For 'min' the
  stored values are STRICTLY INCREASING front -> back (front is the window
  minimum); for 'max' strictly decreasing (front is the maximum). Seqs are always
  strictly increasing front -> back (FIFO insertion order).

Hot surface (push / evictOlderThan are O(1)-AMORTIZED; the reads are O(1)
worst-case; all zero allocation):

- push(v) -> seq          Assign the next monotonic seq, pop all DOMINATED back
                          entries (min: back.value >= v; max: back.value <= v),
                          then append. Returns the assigned seq. Each element is
                          pushed and popped at most once (amortized O(1); a single
                          push is O(k) worst-case). Fail closed: a non-clean value
                          throws [lite-o1] (typeof guard FIRST); a FULL ring throws
                          a byte-identical no-op; a seq past MAX_SEQ (2^53) throws.
- evictOlderThan(seq) -> void  Drop front entries whose stored seq <= seq (the
                          caller's window slide). O(1)-amortized. Validates the seq
                          arg fail-closed (typeof-number guard, NaN rejected).
- value() -> number|undefined   The current window extreme (front value). O(1).
                          undefined on empty, NEVER throws.
- frontSeq() -> number|undefined The seq of the current extreme. O(1). undefined
                          on empty.
- kind (getter)          The frozen 'min' | 'max' invariant.
- size (getter)          Live entry count.
- capacity (getter)      Max simultaneously-live entries (power-of-two, rounded up).
- clear() -> void        O(1): reset head + count + the seq counter, touch NO store
                          (numbers retain no references). The seq counter restarts at 0.
- forEach(fn) -> void    O(k) alloc-free scan front -> back; fn is (value, seq,
                          deque). A documented exception, EXCLUDED from the
                          zero-alloc-per-op claims.
- [Symbol.iterator]()    O(k) scan; the ONE per-protocol ALLOCATOR (yields a
                          [value, seq] tuple + a {value, done} per step) -- OUT of
                          the zero-alloc claims. Use forEach for the alloc-free scan.

Value contract (LOCKED, IDENTICAL to RingDeque): a pushed value must be
typeof 'number' AND not NaN. Rejected (throws [lite-o1]): null, undefined, string,
Symbol, BigInt, object (incl. one with a numeric valueOf), NaN. Accepted: any
finite number, and +Infinity / -Infinity. The typeof guard runs FIRST so a Symbol
/ BigInt never reaches arithmetic.

Windowing model: MonoDeque is a caller-driven PRIMITIVE, not a policy. push
appends and evictOlderThan drops what the caller has slid past, so one MonoDeque
serves any window rule (count-based, time-based, event-based): the deque owns the
monotone invariant, the caller owns which seqs are still in the window.

Amortized honesty: push is O(1) AMORTIZED, not worst-case -- a single push can pop
O(k) dominated back entries. The witness shows the amortized ops/ms staying flat
while a naive O(W)-window-rescan foil collapses, and reports the MAX single-op time
so a hidden worst-case spike shows as a tall bar. MAX_SEQ = 2^53 is the seq
ceiling (seqs live in a Float64 slot; past 2^53 push throws rather than lose
integer precision -- call clear() to reuse).

## MinStack

    new MinStack(capacity, kind)

- capacity: max elements; integer in [1, 2^31]. EXACT -- NOT rounded to a power of
  two (a stack has a linear top pointer, no wrap, no & MASK). The capacity getter
  reports the constructed integer verbatim.
- kind: 'min' or 'max', FROZEN at construction (one extreme per instance).
  Validated fail-closed (anything else throws [lite-o1]). A ctor-cached boolean
  drives the hot compare, so the push body does NO per-call kind-string test.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad capacity (non-integer /
  out-of-range / non-number, typeof-guarded before coercion) or a bad kind.
- Substrate: TWO parallel Float64Arrays -- value[] (the stack) and ext[] (the
  running extreme of everything at/below each index). On push:
  ext[n] = (n===0) ? v : (min: v<ext[n-1]?v:ext[n-1]) (max: v>ext[n-1]?v:ext[n-1]).

Hot surface (all WORST-CASE O(1), zero allocation):

- push(v) -> this         Push v onto the top, carrying the running extreme in ONE
                          compare. Fail closed: a non-clean value throws [lite-o1]
                          (typeof guard FIRST); a FULL stack throws a byte-identical
                          no-op.
- pop() -> number|undefined   Remove+return the TOP; undefined on empty (never
                          throws). Just decrements the top pointer -- the prefix
                          below is already correct, no recompute.
- peek() -> number|undefined  The TOP value without removing it; undefined on empty.
- extreme() -> number|undefined  The current min/max (per the frozen kind) of every
                          live element -- a single running-extreme prefix read.
                          O(1) WORST-CASE. undefined on empty, NEVER throws. Named
                          extreme() (parallels MonoDeque.value()).
- kind (getter)          The frozen 'min' | 'max' extreme.
- size (getter)          Live element count.
- capacity (getter)      Max elements (EXACT, not rounded).
- clear() -> void        O(1): resets the top pointer, touches NO store.
- forEach(fn) -> void    O(k) alloc-free scan TOP -> BOTTOM (pop order); fn is
                          (value, index, stack). A documented exception, EXCLUDED
                          from the zero-alloc-per-op claims.
- [Symbol.iterator]()    O(k) scan TOP -> BOTTOM; ALLOCATES a {value, done} per step
                          by protocol -- OUT of the zero-alloc claims. Use forEach
                          for the alloc-free scan.

Value contract (LOCKED, IDENTICAL to RingDeque / MonoDeque): a pushed value must be
typeof 'number' AND not NaN. Rejected (throws [lite-o1]): null, undefined, string,
Symbol, BigInt, object (incl. one with a numeric valueOf), NaN. Accepted: any
finite number, and +Infinity / -Infinity. The typeof guard runs FIRST so a Symbol
/ BigInt never reaches the compare.

Worst-case honesty: unlike MonoDeque (amortized), MinStack push is WORST-CASE O(1)
-- it never pops a run, so there is no per-op spike to expose. The witness shows a
FLAT extreme() line on a strictly-decreasing feed (its worst case, every push
rewriting ext) with NO MAX-single-op line, because there is nothing to expose.

Memory honesty: the ext[] column DOUBLES the backing memory, so a 2^31 MinStack is
~32 GiB -- the ceiling is a TYPE bound (a legal index fits a Float64 slot), not a
size any host allocates. The throw stays; the note is the disclosure.

## RandomSet

    new RandomSet(universe, capacity = universe, seed = 0x9e3779b1)

- A SUPERSET of SparseSet: it DUPLICATES SparseSet's dense + sparse cross-check
  substrate verbatim (same add / has / delete / clear / forEach / [Symbol.iterator]
  contract), then adds WORST-CASE O(1) uniform sample() + removeRandom().
- universe: exclusive key ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Keys are integers in
  [0, universe).
- capacity: max live members; integer in [1, universe], default universe.
- seed: RNG seed; ANY integer (coerced into the uint32 domain via >>> 0), default
  0x9e3779b1. Validated fail-closed at the ctor door (non-integer / non-number
  throws [lite-o1], typeof-guarded FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches
  coercion). Stored in a per-instance field -- NEVER module-level RNG state.

Hot surface (all WORST-CASE O(1), zero allocation):

- add(k) -> this          Add k (idempotent). Fail closed: a bad key throws
                          [lite-o1]; a new key past capacity throws.
- has(k) -> boolean       True iff k is present. A bad key is ABSENT, never throws.
- delete(k) -> boolean    Remove k (swap-last). Absent/bad key returns false, never
                          throws.
- sample() -> number|undefined  A uniform-random live member WITHOUT removing it
                          (a pure peek of the SET; it DOES advance the RNG word).
                          undefined on empty, NEVER throws.
- removeRandom() -> number|undefined  Remove AND return a uniform-random live member
                          via the same swap-last delete uses (cross-check stays
                          exact). undefined on empty, NEVER throws.
- size (getter)          Live member count.
- capacity (getter)      Max live members as constructed.
- clear() -> void        O(1): resets the count, touches NO store; does NOT reseed.
- forEach(fn) -> void    O(size) alloc-free scan, insertion order; fn is (key, set).
- [Symbol.iterator]()    O(size) scan, insertion order; ALLOCATES per protocol --
                          use forEach for the alloc-free scan.

RNG + bias (LOCKED): the index is the HIGH bits of the advanced NR LCG word --
s = (s * 1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0, then idx = floor(s / 2^32 * n) -- NOT s % n
(the LCG's low bits are weak). NO rejection sampling (it would break worst-case
O(1)); the residual multiply-bias is <= n/2^32 (negligible for any n this substrate
holds) and is DISCLOSED, not coded around. Uniformity is STATISTICAL, not
cryptographic (draw from crypto for adversarial use).

Determinism: the seed is per-instance and defaults to a constant, so two
DEFAULT-seeded RandomSets holding the same members produce IDENTICAL
sample()/removeRandom() sequences -- pass distinct seeds to decorrelate. A given
seed fully reproduces its stream. -0 aliases key 0 via the uint32 coercion.

## FreqO1

    new FreqO1(universe, capacity = universe, maxFreq = 2**32 - 2)

- A WORST-CASE O(1) frequency structure -- the standalone primitive behind O(1) LFU
  eviction. Integer keys [0, universe) are tracked with an access COUNT; the
  least-frequently-used key (lowest count, FIFO tie-break) is peeked / popped in
  O(1) with NO scan.
- universe: exclusive key ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Keys are integers in
  [0, universe).
- capacity: max simultaneously-live keys; integer in [1, universe], default universe.
- maxFreq: the frequency ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32-2], default 2^32-2. Counts live
  in a Uint32 slot, so the ceiling is 2^32-2 (leaving room for the freq+1 write); an
  increment past maxFreq throws [lite-o1] rather than wrap.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad universe / capacity / maxFreq
  (typeof-guarded FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches coercion; String(x) message).
- Substrate (all PRIVATE Uint32Array columns; NO public SlotPool -- ADR 0003's
  deferral stands, FreqO1 owns its own node pool + stays self-contained): KEYS ride
  SparseSet's dense + sparse cross-check (dense index = the stable node id). Per KEY:
  freq, bucket-of, and next/prev intrusive DOUBLY-linked list within a bucket (FIFO).
  Per BUCKET (a 1-based bump + free-stack pool, bucket 0 = NIL): the frequency it
  represents, prev/next in a list sorted ASCENDING by frequency, and FIFO head/tail
  key nodes. `_head` = the min-frequency bucket, so peekMin / popMin are O(1).

Hot surface (all WORST-CASE O(1), zero allocation):

- add(k) -> this          Ensure k is tracked at frequency 1 if absent; IDEMPOTENT
                          no-op if already present (does NOT bump). Fail closed: a bad
                          key throws [lite-o1]; a NEW key past capacity throws.
- increment(k) -> this    Record one access: insert at frequency 1 if absent, else
                          frequency += 1. Fail closed: a bad key throws; a NEW key
                          past capacity throws; a bump past maxFreq throws. Every
                          throw is a byte-identical no-op.
- frequencyOf(k) -> number  k's current frequency, or 0 if absent / bad key. NEVER
                          throws (0 = not tracked is the correct frequency).
- has(k) -> boolean       True iff k is tracked. A bad key is ABSENT, never throws.
- peekMin() -> number|undefined  The least-frequently-used key (lowest frequency;
                          FIFO tie-break -- earliest-inserted in that bucket) WITHOUT
                          removing it. undefined on empty, NEVER throws.
- popMin() -> number|undefined  Remove AND return the least-frequently-used key (same
                          selection as peekMin). undefined on empty, NEVER throws.
- size (getter)          Live key count.
- capacity (getter)      Max simultaneously-live keys as constructed.
- universe (getter)      Exclusive key ceiling.
- maxFrequency (getter)  The frequency ceiling.
- clear() -> void        O(1): resets the live count + the bucket-list head + the
                          bucket pool (bump + free stack) -- four scalars, touches NO
                          store (stale dense/sparse fail the has() cross-check).
- forEach(fn) -> void    O(size) alloc-free scan in DENSE STORAGE order (insertion
                          order, permuted by a popMin swap-remove -- NOT frequency
                          order); fn is (key, frequency, freq). Re-reads size each
                          step, so a re-entrant popMin self-terminates.
- [Symbol.iterator]()    O(size) scan, same order; ALLOCATES per protocol -- use
                          forEach for the alloc-free scan.

Lean LFU surface (LOCKED): NO decrement, NO peekMax, NO delete(k). Fail closed on
the MUTATORS (add / increment throw [lite-o1] on a bad key, typeof-guarded before
the coercing >>>; null is not zero); ABSENT on the QUERIES (has / frequencyOf never
throw). peekMin / popMin on an empty structure return undefined (never throw).

Bucket-pool sizing (why free-list exhaustion cannot occur): non-empty buckets
partition the live keys by frequency, so at REST there are <= size <= capacity of
them. A single increment TRANSIENTLY creates the target bucket BEFORE freeing an
emptied source, peaking at size + 1 <= capacity + 1. The pool therefore holds
capacity + 1 usable buckets, so exhaustion CANNOT happen under the contract; the
_poolExhausted throw is a fail-closed guard, defense in depth, never reached.

Worst-case honesty: like MinStack / RandomSet, every hot op is WORST-CASE O(1) (a
fixed number of pointer writes on the bucket forest, never a run) -- so the witness
prints NO MAX-single-op line; the flat line IS the worst-case claim.

## BucketQueue

    new BucketQueue(universe, ceiling, capacity = universe)

- An AMORTIZED O(1) MONOTONE integer priority queue -- the standalone primitive behind
  Dial's algorithm (Dijkstra over small integer priorities). Integer keys [0, universe)
  are inserted at an integer priority [0, ceiling]; extractMin drains keys in
  NON-DECREASING priority order (FIFO tie-break within a priority).
- universe: exclusive key ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Keys are integers in [0, universe).
- ceiling: INCLUSIVE max priority; integer in [0, 2^31-1]. Priorities are [0, ceiling].
  Space is O(ceiling) -- a documented co-headline: the static per-priority bucket arrays
  are length ceiling+1. The 2^31-1 bound is a TYPE bound (an ~8 GiB bucket column), not a
  practical size; a bucket queue is FOR small bounded integer priorities.
- capacity: max simultaneously-live keys; integer in [1, universe], default universe.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad universe / ceiling / capacity
  (typeof-guarded FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches coercion; String(x) message).
- Substrate (all PRIVATE Uint32Array columns; NO public SlotPool -- ADR 0003's deferral
  stands): KEYS ride SparseSet's dense + sparse cross-check (dense index = the stable
  node id). Per KEY: priority (== its bucket index) + next/prev intrusive FIFO list
  within a bucket. Per BUCKET (a STATIC array indexed by priority 0..ceiling, NO
  free-list): FIFO head/tail key nodes. A scalar cursor `_cur` is the monotone frontier;
  extractMin / peekMin advance it FORWARD over emptied buckets to the min non-empty
  bucket. clear() is O(1): a stale static bucket head is voided by the SAME `i < _n`
  cross-check that voids stale sparse entries (a bucket p is non-empty iff
  _bHead[p] < _n && _prio[_bHead[p]] === p), so no per-bucket reset is needed.

Hot surface (all AMORTIZED O(1), zero allocation):

- insert(k, p) -> this      Insert k at priority p. IDEMPOTENT no-op if k is already
                            present (use decreaseKey to lower it). Fail closed: a bad
                            key / bad priority / a priority BELOW the cursor / a NEW key
                            past capacity throw [lite-o1] as a byte-identical no-op.
- decreaseKey(k, newPrio) -> this  Lower k's priority. An ABSENT key, or a newPrio that
                            is NOT a strict decrease, is a documented no-op (the
                            conventional relaxation semantics -- decreaseKey only ever
                            lowers). Fail closed: a bad key / bad priority / a newPrio
                            BELOW the cursor throw [lite-o1] as a byte-identical no-op.
- extractMin() -> number|undefined  Remove + return the min-priority key (FIFO tie-break).
                            Advances the cursor FORWARD (never rewinds). undefined on
                            empty, NEVER throws.
- peekMin() -> number|undefined  The min-priority key without removing it. undefined on
                            empty, NEVER throws.
- priorityOf(k) -> number   k's priority, or -1 if absent / bad key. NEVER throws (-1 is
                            the unambiguous "not tracked" sentinel; every real priority
                            is a non-negative integer in [0, ceiling]).
- has(k) -> boolean         True iff k is tracked. A bad key is ABSENT, never throws.
- size / capacity / universe / ceiling / cursor (getters).
- clear() -> void           O(1): resets the live count + the cursor to 0; touches NO
                            store (stale dense/sparse + static buckets fail the cross-check).
- forEach(fn) -> void       O(size) alloc-free scan in DENSE STORAGE order (NOT priority
                            order); fn is (key, priority, queue). Re-reads size each step,
                            so a re-entrant extractMin self-terminates.
- [Symbol.iterator]()       O(size) scan, same order; ALLOCATES per protocol -- use
                            forEach for the alloc-free scan.

MONOTONE contract (LOCKED -- this is what buys the amortized O(1)): the extract order is
non-decreasing and the cursor NEVER rewinds. insert(k, p) with p < cursor, and
decreaseKey(k, newPrio) with newPrio < cursor, both THROW [lite-o1] (fail-closed,
byte-identical no-op before the throw). Because the cursor only moves forward, its total
travel across a full drain is <= ceiling+1, so the per-extractMin bucket scan amortizes to
O(1) even though a single extractMin is O(gap) worst-case (the amortized-not-worst-case
honesty, like MonoDeque / UnionFind). Guards use `>=` (p >= ceiling+1) / `<` (p < cursor)
/ `===` (n === capacity), all fail-closed.

Key / priority model: keys integer [0, universe); priorities integer [0, ceiling]. Both
guards are typeof-first (`typeof x !== 'number' || (x >>> 0) !== x || x >= bound`) so a
Symbol / BigInt never reaches the coercing `>>>`; messages via String(x). null is not
zero. Fail closed on the MUTATORS (insert / decreaseKey), ABSENT on the QUERIES (has /
priorityOf never throw). -0 aliases key 0 AND priority 0 via the uint32 coercion.

Pool sizing (why exhaustion is impossible under contract, yet still fails closed): at most
capacity keys are live at once, one node slot per key (dense / prio / nk / pk are all
capacity-sized), so the `n === capacity` guard rejects a NEW key past capacity as a
byte-identical no-op and no node slot is ever over-allocated. The buckets are static
(0..ceiling), so there is no bucket free-list to exhaust.

## TimerWheel

    new TimerWheel(universe, slots, capacity = universe)

- A WORST-CASE O(1) BOUNDED "simple" timing wheel (Varghese-Lauck's single-wheel
  variant, NOT the hashed / hierarchical one). Integer timer ids [0, universe) are
  scheduled against a monotone tick clock: scheduling id with delay d files it into
  slot[(now + d) & MASK] until fired or canceled. Delay is bounded to [0, slots-1] (the
  documented range ceiling); space is O(capacity + slots).
- universe: exclusive id ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Ids are integers in [0, universe).
- slots: number of wheel slots; integer in [1, 2^31], ROUNDED UP to the next power of two
  (the getter reports the rounded value; MASK = slots-1). Space is O(slots) -- the honest
  bounded-delay-range co-headline (parallel to BucketQueue's ceiling). The 2^31 bound is a
  TYPE bound, not a practical size; a simple wheel is FOR a bounded delay horizon.
- capacity: max simultaneously-live timers; integer in [1, universe], default universe.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad universe / slots / capacity
  (typeof-guarded FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches coercion; String(x) message).
- Substrate (all PRIVATE Uint32Array columns; NO public SlotPool -- ADR 0003's deferral
  stands): IDS ride SparseSet's dense + sparse cross-check (dense index = the stable node
  id). Per NODE: slotOf (which slot it is in) + next/prev intrusive FIFO list within a
  slot. Per SLOT (a STATIC array indexed 0..slots-1, NO free-list): FIFO head/tail nodes.
  clear() is O(1): a stale static slot head is voided by the SAME `i < _size` cross-check
  that voids stale sparse entries (a slot s is non-empty iff
  _sHead[s] < _size && _slotOf[_sHead[s]] === s), so no per-slot reset is needed.

Hot surface (schedule / cancel / advance(1) / has WORST-CASE O(1); drainDue O(due); all
zero allocation):

- schedule(id, delay) -> this  File id into slot[(now + delay) & MASK]. IDEMPOTENT no-op
                            if id is already present (reschedule = cancel then schedule).
                            Fail closed: a bad id / a delay >= slots / a NEW id past
                            capacity throw [lite-o1] as a byte-identical no-op.
- cancel(id) -> boolean     Unlink id from its slot FIFO + swap-remove. True iff it was
                            scheduled; a bad / absent id returns false, NEVER throws.
- drainDue(fn) -> void      Fire + remove EXACTLY the timers present in the due slot
                            (slot[now & MASK]) at ENTRY, calling fn(id, wheel) in FIFO
                            order. O(due). SNAPSHOT semantics: a timer (re)scheduled during
                            fn DEFERS to a later drainDue (a self-reschedule-at-0 fires once
                            this drain then defers -> always terminates; periodic idiom =
                            reschedule at delay >= 1); a timer canceled during fn before it
                            fires does NOT fire. Re-entrant schedule/cancel/clear from
                            inside fn are supported (the due list is moved into a reserved
                            DRAINING identity at entry, then head-drained); re-entrant
                            ADVANCE throws (see advance). fn is user code -- the one
                            documented alloc exception.
- advance(ticks = 1) -> this  FAIL-CLOSED drain-before-advance: every slot left behind
                            must be EMPTY (drained), else it throws [lite-o1] as a
                            byte-identical no-op. Also throws if called from INSIDE a drainDue
                            callback (an in-flight drain -- advancing would strand the
                            un-fired due timers). advance(1) is worst-case O(1) (one
                            emptiness check + a counter add); advance(k) is O(k) checks.
                            ticks is [0, 2^32-1]; `now` is capped at 2^53 via a `>=` guard.
- has(id) -> boolean        True iff id is scheduled. A bad id is ABSENT, never throws.
- size / capacity / universe / slots / now (getters).
- clear() -> void           O(1): resets the live count + the tick clock to 0; touches NO
                            store (stale dense/sparse + static slot heads fail the cross-check).
- forEach(fn) -> void       O(size) alloc-free scan in DENSE STORAGE order (NOT time
                            order); fn is (id, slot, wheel). Re-reads size each step, so a
                            re-entrant cancel self-terminates.
- [Symbol.iterator]()       O(size) scan, same order; ALLOCATES per protocol -- use
                            forEach for the alloc-free scan.

DRAIN-BEFORE-ADVANCE contract (LOCKED -- this is what buys the worst-case O(1) with NO
max-single-op line): slot[now & MASK] IS the due set; advance() refuses to lap the wheel
over an undrained slot (it throws fail-closed). Because a slot is never advanced past
while non-empty, a slot always holds exactly one rotation's timers -- so there is NO
cursor, NO absolute-deadline column, and NO O(gap) worst case (unlike BucketQueue). The
`now` ceiling guard uses `>=` (now + ticks >= 2^53 throws) -- the MonoDeque
saturating-counter lesson, primed by a white-box test; a `>` would be off-by-one.

Id / delay / ticks model: ids integer [0, universe); delay integer [0, slots-1]; ticks
integer [0, 2^32-1]. Every guard is typeof-first (`typeof x !== 'number' ||
(x >>> 0) !== x || x >= bound`) on BOTH the id and the delay/ticks arg, so a Symbol /
BigInt never reaches the coercing `>>>`; messages via String(x). null is not zero. Fail
closed on the MUTATORS (schedule / advance), ABSENT on the QUERIES (has / cancel never
throw). -0 aliases id 0 AND delay 0 via the uint32 coercion.

Pool sizing (why exhaustion is impossible under contract, yet still fails closed): at most
capacity ids are live at once, one node slot per id (dense / slotOf / next / prev are all
capacity-sized), so the `size === capacity` guard rejects a NEW id past capacity as a
byte-identical no-op and no node slot is ever over-allocated. The slots are static
(0..slots-1), so there is no slot free-list to exhaust.

## HierarchicalTimerWheel

    new HierarchicalTimerWheel(universe, capacity = universe)

- An AMORTIZED O(1) CASCADING timing wheel -- the multi-level sibling of TimerWheel. Where
  a simple wheel holds one rotation's timers (delay <= slots-1), this nests FOUR levels in
  the Linux tvec shape and cascades coarse timers down to finer levels as the clock
  advances, so it schedules a far larger BOUNDED delay horizon (delay in [0, 2^26)) with the
  SAME zero-alloc substrate -- one node per timer, moved between intrusive lists BY INDEX.
- universe: exclusive id ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Ids are integers in [0, universe).
- capacity: max simultaneously-live timers; integer in [1, universe], default universe.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad universe / capacity (typeof-guarded
  FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches coercion; String(x) message).
- GEOMETRY (hybrid 1x256 + 3x64, total range 2^26): level 0 = 256 slots (mask 0xFF, shift
  0), scanned every drainDue tick -- the hot path; levels 1..3 = 64 slots each (mask 0x3F,
  shifts 8/14/20), covering delay in [2^8, 2^14), [2^14, 2^20), [2^20, 2^26). Level/slot for
  a timer expiring at `expiry` with delta = expiry - now: delta < 2^8 -> L0 slot
  expiry & 0xFF; < 2^14 -> L1 (expiry >>> 8) & 0x3F; < 2^20 -> L2 (expiry >>> 14) & 0x3F;
  else L3 (expiry >>> 20) & 0x3F.
- Substrate (all PRIVATE; mirrors TimerWheel's, diverging only where the multi-level heads
  require it): IDS ride SparseSet's dense + sparse cross-check (dense index = node id). Per
  NODE: listOf (the flat list it sits in, 0..447 or the DRAINING identity 448), next/prev
  intrusive FIFO, and expiry (a Float64, integer-exact to 2^53, needed to re-file on
  cascade). Per LIST (a STATIC array of length 449, NO free-list): FIFO head/tail. clear()
  is O(1): stale heads are voided by the SAME cross-check that voids stale sparse entries.

Hot surface (schedule / cancel / advance(1) / has AMORTIZED O(1); drainDue O(due); all zero
allocation):

- schedule(id, delay) -> this  File id at the level/slot for `delay` (expiry = now + delay).
                            IDEMPOTENT no-op if present. Fail closed: a bad id / a delay >=
                            2^26 / a NEW id past capacity / an expiry reaching 2^53 throw
                            [lite-o1] as a byte-identical no-op.
- cancel(id) -> boolean     Unlink id + swap-remove. True iff scheduled; a bad / absent id
                            returns false, NEVER throws.
- drainDue(fn) -> void      Fire + remove every timer in the level-0 due list
                            (slot[now & 0xFF]) at ENTRY, fn(id, wheel) in FIFO order. O(due).
                            SNAPSHOT semantics identical to TimerWheel (re-entrant
                            schedule/cancel/clear supported; the due list is moved into the
                            reserved DRAINING identity then head-drained; a re-entrant
                            advance throws). fn is user code -- the one alloc exception.
- advance(ticks = 1) -> this  DRAIN-BEFORE-CASCADE: each level-0 slot left behind must be
                            EMPTY or it throws [lite-o1]. On a level-0 wrap (every 256 ticks)
                            the next level's due bucket is CASCADED down (nested for levels
                            2/3). advance(1) is O(1) on a normal tick and O(levels + bucket)
                            on a wrap -- the max-single-op cascade SPIKE (the teaching
                            feature; the witness prints it), amortized O(1) over a timer's
                            life. Also throws [lite-o1] on `now` reaching 2^53, or a
                            re-entrant advance (nested / in-flight drain, via a _busy guard).
- has(id) -> boolean        True iff scheduled. A bad id is ABSENT, never throws.
- size / capacity / universe / now / maxDelay (getters). maxDelay is 2^26 - 1.
- clear() -> void           O(1): resets the live count + tick clock to 0; touches NO store.
- forEach(fn) -> void       O(size) alloc-free scan in DENSE STORAGE order (NOT time order);
                            fn is (id, expiry, wheel). Re-reads size each step, so a
                            re-entrant cancel self-terminates.
- [Symbol.iterator]()       O(size) scan, same order; ALLOCATES per protocol -- use forEach
                            for the alloc-free scan.

CASCADE contract (LOCKED -- the zero-GC crux + the amortized O(1)): a level-1 due bucket
always has delta < 256 by the wrap that cascades it, so it re-files into level 0; a level-2
bucket into level 1/0; a level-3 bucket into level 2/1/0 -- always a FINER (different) list,
so the emptied source is cleared and the walk terminates, all by INDEX (ZERO allocation).
Each timer cascades at most levels-1 times over its life, so advance amortizes to O(1) per
tick even though a wrap tick is O(bucket). The foil is a FAIR one -- an alloc-free 4-ary
min-heap (O(log n) per tick) -- not a strawman; the wheel wins by an O(1) constant while
wearing the cascade spike (see the witness + ADR 0015).

Id / delay / ticks model: ids integer [0, universe); delay integer [0, 2^26); ticks integer
[0, 2^32-1]. Every guard is typeof-first so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches the coercing
`>>>`; messages via String(x). null is not zero. Fail closed on the MUTATORS (schedule /
advance throw), ABSENT on the QUERIES (has / cancel never throw). Re-entrant advance is the
one drainDue-callback exception -- it throws [lite-o1] (schedule / cancel / clear stay legal).

## CoarseTimerWheel

    new CoarseTimerWheel(universe, capacity = universe)

- A WORST-CASE O(1), NON-CASCADING, near-unbounded timing wheel with an APPROXIMATE (bounded,
  one-sided-LATE) fire time -- the Linux-4.8 coarse-bucket model. The third wheel: TimerWheel
  is bounded + EXACT + worst-case; HierarchicalTimerWheel is bounded 2^26 + EXACT + AMORTIZED
  (cascade spike); CoarseTimerWheel is near-unbounded + APPROXIMATE + worst-case with NO
  cascade and NO max-single-op line. A far-future timer sits in a COARSE bucket and fires IN
  PLACE -- never cascaded, never re-filed. HEADLINE TRADE: precision for range -- a timer fires
  LATE by at most gran(level) - 1 (<= 12.5% relative error, ONE-SIDED never early; L0 EXACT).
  For EXACT far-future deadlines use a min-heap (@zakkster/lite-logn); the classic
  hashed-with-rounds wheel is REJECTED (expected-O(1) / worst-case-O(n), see ADR 0022).
- universe: exclusive id ceiling; integer in [1, 2^32]. Ids are integers in [0, universe).
- capacity: max simultaneously-live timers; integer in [1, universe], default universe.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a bad universe / capacity (typeof-guarded FIRST
  so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches coercion; String(x) message).
- GEOMETRY: 9 levels x 64 buckets, per-level clock shift 3n, granularity g_n = 8^n (L0 = 1
  EXACT, L1 = 8, ..., L8 = 2^24). Horizon MAX_DELAY = 62 x 2^24 = 0x3E000000 = 1,040,187,392
  (~0.97 x 2^30); delay in [0, MAX_DELAY). The horizon is a Linux WHEEL_TIMEOUT_MAX phase
  margin below the full 2^30 L8 span so the top level's 64 buckets never overflow (delta_8 <= 63
  at every clock phase). The monotone tick clock is capped at 2^53.
- FIRE-TIME BOUND (round-up-then-verify select): schedule rounds the deadline (now + delay) UP
  to the finest level granularity whose granule-delta ceil(deadline/g_n) - floor(now/g_n) lands
  in [0, 63], escalating to the next coarser level otherwise. The applied fire tick
  F = ceil(deadline/g_n) x g_n obeys now+delay <= F < now+delay + g_n. Because escalation keeps
  delta <= 63 < 64, a bucket's FIRST visit IS its fire tick (no aliasing) -- so drain / peekNext
  / advance stay pure-BITMAP O(1), never reading _fireAt.
- Substrate (all PRIVATE): IDS ride SparseSet's dense + sparse cross-check (dense index = node
  id). Per NODE: bucketOf (flat bucket 0..575 or the DRAINING identity 576), next/prev intrusive
  FIFO, and fireAt (a Float64, integer-exact to 2^53 -- WRITTEN by schedule, READ only by
  fireTimeOf). Per BUCKET: a STATIC head/tail array of length 577; a bucket is non-empty iff its
  _bits bit is set. _bits is a per-bucket occupancy BITMAP (18 x Uint32 = 576 bits; level n in
  words [2n, 2n+2)) driving find-first-set for advance / drainDue / peekNext.

Hot surface (schedule / cancel / advance(k) worst-case O(1); drainDue O(due + levels); all zero
allocation):

- schedule(id, delay) -> this  Place id at the level/bucket for `delay` (fire >= now + delay,
                            late by <= gran(level) - 1). IDEMPOTENT no-op if present. Fail
                            closed: a bad id / a delay >= MAX_DELAY / a NEW id past capacity /
                            a deadline or fire tick reaching 2^53 throw [lite-o1] as a
                            byte-identical no-op.
- cancel(id) -> boolean     Unlink id + swap-remove (clearing the bucket bit if it empties).
                            True iff scheduled; a bad / absent id returns false, NEVER throws.
- drainDue(fn) -> void      Fire + remove every timer DUE at the current tick, FINEST-FIRST
                            across levels (each level n with now % g_n === 0, bucket
                            (now / g_n) % 64), fn(id, wheel) in FIFO order. O(due + levels).
                            SNAPSHOT semantics (each due bucket is moved into the reserved
                            DRAINING identity then head-drained; a re-entrant (re)schedule
                            DEFERS to a later drain; re-entrant cancel/clear supported; a
                            re-entrant advance throws). fn is user code -- the one alloc exception.
- advance(ticks = 1) -> this  DRAIN-BEFORE-ADVANCE, worst-case O(1) for ANY k (no per-tick
                            loop, no cascade): validates via the bitmap that no due timer lies
                            in [now, now+ticks) (peekNext empty or >= now+ticks) else throws
                            [lite-o1] as a byte-identical no-op. Also throws on `now` reaching
                            2^53, or a re-entrant advance (nested / in-flight drain, via _busy).
                            NO max-single-op line (worst-case cohort).
- peekNext() -> number      The next tick any timer is due (bitmap find-first-set across the 9
                            levels), or -1 when empty. O(1), never throws.
- fireTimeOf(id) -> number  The applied (rounded) fire tick for a scheduled id, or -1 for an
                            absent / bad id. O(1), never throws. fireTimeOf(id) - (schedule-time
                            now + delay) is the one-sided lateness, in [0, gran(level) - 1].
- has(id) -> boolean        True iff scheduled. A bad id is ABSENT, never throws.
- size / capacity / universe / now / maxDelay (getters). maxDelay is MAX_DELAY - 1.
- clear() -> void           O(1): resets the live count + tick clock to 0 and clears the 18-word
                            occupancy bitmap (a FIXED fill, NOT an O(horizon) sweep).
- forEach(fn) -> void       O(size) alloc-free scan in DENSE STORAGE order (NOT time order);
                            fn is (id, fireAt, wheel). Re-reads size each step, so a re-entrant
                            cancel self-terminates.
- [Symbol.iterator]()       O(size) scan, same order; ALLOCATES per protocol -- use forEach.

Id / delay / ticks model: ids integer [0, universe); delay integer [0, MAX_DELAY); ticks integer
[0, 2^32-1]. Every guard is typeof-first so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches the coercing `>>>`;
messages via String(x). null is not zero. Fail closed on the MUTATORS (schedule / advance throw),
ABSENT on the QUERIES (has / cancel / peekNext / fireTimeOf never throw). Re-entrant advance is
the one drainDue-callback exception -- it throws [lite-o1] (schedule / cancel / clear stay legal).

## RingLog

    new RingLog(capacity)

- A WORST-CASE O(1) fixed-capacity LOSSY overwrite-oldest ring log -- "keep the last N".
  push never blocks and never throws on full: a full push OVERWRITES the oldest entry
  and RETURNS it. This INVERTS RingDeque's fail-closed-on-full policy; the two are a
  teaching pair (lossy-overwrite vs fail-closed-at-capacity). It mirrors RingDeque's
  substrate EXACTLY -- ONE Float64Array, head (index of the oldest) + count, power-of-two
  capacity, branchless & MASK wrap.
- capacity: requested max entries; integer in [1, 2^31]. ROUNDS UP to the next power of
  two (>= requested); the capacity getter reports the rounded value.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / out-of-range / non-number
  arg (typeof-guarded before any coercion; message via String(x)).
- Substrate: ONE Float64Array (numeric values only). The physical slot for logical offset
  i from the oldest is buf[(head + i) & MASK], MASK = capacity - 1; wrap is a single &
  (power-of-two modulo), no branch. Object payloads are the caller's problem: push an
  integer handle and keep the payload in a parallel SoA column keyed by it.

Hot surface (all WORST-CASE O(1), zero allocation):

- push(v) -> number|undefined  Append v as the NEWEST entry. Returns the EVICTED oldest
                        value when the log was FULL (v overwrote it), or undefined while
                        the log is still filling. NEVER throws when full (it overwrites);
                        throws [lite-o1] on a non-clean value (typeof guard FIRST; a full
                        bad push is a byte-identical no-op). The return value is the
                        signature feature -- a rolling-aggregate hook (subtract-evicted,
                        add-new). WORST-CASE O(1): a full push is a single read + a single
                        overwrite + a head advance, never a run -> NO amortized spike, NO
                        max-single-op line (RingLog is in the worst-case cohort).
- get(i) -> number|undefined   The entry at OLDEST-relative index i (0 oldest .. size-1
                        newest). O(1). A non-integer or out-of-range i returns undefined,
                        NEVER throws (typeof-first so a Symbol / BigInt never coerces).
- oldest() -> number|undefined The OLDEST live entry. O(1). undefined on empty.
- newest() -> number|undefined The NEWEST live entry. O(1). undefined on empty.
- size / capacity (rounded) / isFull (getters). isFull is count === capacity.
- clear() -> void       O(1): resets head + count, touches NO store (numbers retain no
                        references, so nothing to zero -- mirrors RingDeque).
- forEach(fn) -> void   O(size) alloc-free scan OLDEST -> NEWEST; fn is (value, index, log).
- [Symbol.iterator]()   O(size) scan OLDEST -> NEWEST; the ONE per-protocol ALLOCATOR --
                        use forEach for the alloc-free scan.

Value contract (LOCKED, IDENTICAL to RingDeque): a pushed value must be typeof 'number'
AND not NaN. Rejected (throws [lite-o1]): null, undefined, string, Symbol, BigInt, object
(incl. one with a numeric valueOf), NaN. Accepted: any finite number, and +Infinity /
-Infinity. The typeof guard runs FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches arithmetic.

Read-only vs consumable (LOCKED): RingLog is a rolling window you READ (a snapshot
surface), NOT a queue you CONSUME -- there is deliberately NO popOldest / drain. Reach
for RingDeque when you need to drain entries or fail closed at capacity; reach for RingLog
when you want to keep only the last N and never block.

## CuckooMap

    new CuckooMap(capacity, seed?)

- A bounded-probe EXACT map from GENERAL INTEGER keys to numbers -- the suite's first
  general-key dictionary. Keys are ANY safe integer (|k| <= 2^53, Number.isSafeInteger
  range), NOT a dense [0, universe) like SparseSet: CuckooMap costs O(capacity) space over a
  SPARSE / large integer key domain, versus SparseSet's O(universe) over a dense one. Values
  are any finite number plus +/-Infinity (typeof 'number', not NaN), in a Float64 column.
  Keys and values are numbers ONLY -- the zero-GC law forbids object / string references
  (map them to integer handles).
- Algorithm: BUCKETIZED cuckoo hashing, 2 tables x 4 slots. A lookup probes AT MOST 8 slots
  ALWAYS -> HARD bounded-probe WORST-CASE O(1) for get / has / delete. set is AMORTIZED O(1):
  a full home-bucket pair kicks a resident to its alternate bucket (an eviction chain bounded
  by MaxLoop = 8*log2(cap)), and on a MaxLoop dead end ONE in-place O(capacity) RE-SEED (a
  fresh per-instance seed + re-insert of every live entry) -- the member's MAX-SINGLE-OP line,
  the thematic sibling of HierarchicalTimerWheel's cascade spike.
- capacity: requested max live entries; integer in [1, 2^30]. The constructor rounds the
  bucket count up (power of two) so the request fits UNDER a 0.90 load ceiling; the capacity
  getter reports the usable capacity. seed: OPTIONAL uint32 for reproducible placement,
  defaults deterministically.
- Fixed capacity, fail closed: a set of a NEW key past the 0.90 ceiling, or one the eviction
  chain + re-seed cannot place, throws [lite-o1] (the load-ceiling reject is a byte-identical
  no-op). No silent growth.
- Sentinel discipline: 0 is a LEGAL key and any finite number a legal value. Emptiness is
  signalled ONLY by a Uint8Array occupancy column, NEVER by a 0 key / value ("null is not
  zero"). Deletion clears the occupancy byte -- cuckoo needs no tombstones.
- Hash: an inline murmur-style int32 finalizer over the 53-bit key (low 32 bits + high 21
  bits + sign) with two decorrelated per-instance seeds, all int32 math (no coercion, no heap
  double).

Hot surface:

- set(k, v) -> this        Insert / update. AMORTIZED O(1), zero-alloc on the common path.
                        Guards typeof of BOTH k and v FIRST (a Symbol / BigInt / object never
                        coerces); a bad key / value throws [lite-o1] a byte-identical no-op. An
                        UPDATE of a present key overwrites the value (no eviction, size
                        unchanged). A NEW key past the ceiling / an unplaceable key throws
                        [lite-o1] fail closed. The in-place re-seed is the max-single-op spike.
- get(k) -> number|undefined  WORST-CASE O(1), <= 8 slot reads. A bad / absent key -> undefined,
                        NEVER throws (typeof-first).
- has(k) -> boolean     WORST-CASE O(1). A bad / absent key -> false, never throws.
- delete(k) -> boolean  WORST-CASE O(1): clears the occupancy byte, decrements size. true iff
                        present; never throws.
- clear() -> void       O(capacity): zeroes the occupancy signal (a Uint8Array fill), resets
                        size. The key / value columns are left as stale, unreachable numbers.
- size / capacity (usable) / seed (uint32) / load (size/capacity) -- getters.
- forEach(fn) -> void   O(capacity) alloc-free scan in DENSE SLOT order; fn is (key, value, map).
- [Symbol.iterator]()   O(capacity) scan yielding [key, value] tuples; the ONE per-protocol
                        ALLOCATOR -- use forEach for the alloc-free scan.

Key / value contract (LOCKED): a key must be typeof 'number' AND Number.isSafeInteger
(|k| <= 2^53); a value must be typeof 'number' AND not NaN (+/-Infinity accepted). Rejected on
set (throws [lite-o1], a byte-identical no-op): null, undefined, string, Symbol, BigInt, object
(incl. one with a numeric valueOf), NaN, a non-safe-integer key. The typeof guard runs FIRST so
a Symbol / BigInt never reaches arithmetic. -0 aliases key 0.

SparseSet vs CuckooMap (the space contrast): SparseSet is an O(universe)-space DENSE integer
SET (membership only) over a bounded [0, universe); CuckooMap is an O(capacity)-space exact MAP
(key -> number) over SPARSE / large integer keys. Pick SparseSet when keys are dense + bounded
and you need only membership; pick CuckooMap when keys are sparse / large and you need values.
(For APPROXIMATE membership with false positives, reach for @zakkster/lite-filter instead.)

## SparseTable

    new SparseTable(source, kind)

- A WORST-CASE O(1)-QUERY STATIC range-minimum / range-maximum table (the classic
  idempotent-operation sparse table / "StaticRMQ") -- the suite's FIRST static build-once /
  immutable member. Build the table ONCE, then answer "the min (or max) over [l, r]" in true
  worst-case O(1) forever.
- source: the values to index; a real Array of numbers OR any numeric TypedArray, length in
  [1, 2^26]. COPIED element-by-element into an internal Float64Array at build, so a later
  mutation of the caller's array can NEVER invalidate a query (genuinely immutable +
  self-contained). Object / string / BigInt-typed sources fail the per-element number check.
- kind: 'min' or 'max', FROZEN at construction (one extreme per instance; run TWO instances for
  both -- mirrors MinStack / MonoDeque). A ctor-cached boolean drives the hot compare, so
  query() does NO per-call kind-string test.
- Constructor throws a [lite-o1] error on a non-array / empty / bad-length source, a bad kind,
  or a non-numeric / NaN element (typeof-guarded FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never coerces;
  String(x) message). Nothing half-built escapes -- validation throws before the table is
  allocated or any instance field is assigned; the source-copy scratch buffer is a discarded
  local, so a throw leaves nothing queryable (a byte-identical no-op).

THE HONESTY CONTRACT (the load-bearing decision -- see decisions/0018): the QUERY is the hot op
and it is TRUE WORST-CASE O(1), zero-alloc. The O(n log n) BUILD and the O(n log n) table SPACE
are a DISCLOSED CO-HEADLINE (the same shape as BucketQueue's O(ceiling) space, TimerWheel's
O(slots), HierarchicalTimerWheel's O(capacity)): paid ONCE at construction, EXCLUDED from the
per-op claim. The witness gates the QUERY; build is never in the measured window. Because the
query is worst-case O(1) (not amortized), there is NO max-single-op line.

Layout (flat SoA): ONE internal Float64Array copy of the n source values + ONE flat
Float64Array `_table` of length n*(K+1) where K = floor(log2(n)) (levels 0..K), indexed manually
as table[level*n + i] = the extreme over the span [i, i+2^level). Level 0 is the source; level j
folds two level-(j-1) spans of 2^(j-1). EXACT SPACE co-headline: n*(floor(log2 n)+1) table cells
+ n source cells = n*(floor(log2 n)+2) Float64 slots.

Hot surface (query / at are WORST-CASE O(1), zero allocation):

- query(l, r) -> number|undefined  The extreme (min or max, per the frozen kind) over the
                        INCLUSIVE range [l, r]. WORST-CASE O(1): one floor-log2 (via clz32) + two
                        table reads + one compare (the idempotent-overlap trick -- two
                        overlapping 2^k-wide windows cover [l, r] exactly even where they
                        overlap). A bad l / r (non-number, non-int, out of [0, length), or l > r)
                        returns undefined and NEVER throws (the family "queries never throw" law;
                        typeof FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never coerces).
- at(i) -> number|undefined  The single source element at index i. O(1). undefined out of range /
                        non-integer, NEVER throws (symmetry with query).
- length (getter)       Number of source elements.
- kind (getter)         The frozen 'min' | 'max' extreme.
- forEach(fn) -> void   O(length) alloc-free scan of the SOURCE values in index order; fn is
                        (value, index, table). A documented exception, EXCLUDED from the
                        zero-alloc-per-op claims.
- [Symbol.iterator]()   O(length) scan of the source values; the ONE per-protocol ALLOCATOR --
                        use forEach for the alloc-free scan.

Build-once, query-only (LOCKED): there are NO mutators (no set / update / push) and NO clear() --
the table is immutable, so a clear would be nonsensical (see the ADR). Rebuild a new instance to
change the data.

Value contract (LOCKED, IDENTICAL to RingDeque / MonoDeque / MinStack / RingLog): every source
element must be typeof 'number' AND not NaN. Rejected (throws [lite-o1] at construction): null,
undefined, string, Symbol, BigInt, object (incl. one with a numeric valueOf), NaN. Accepted: any
finite number, and +Infinity / -Infinity. The typeof guard runs FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never
reaches coercion.

Worst-case honesty: like MinStack / RingLog, the query is WORST-CASE O(1) -- so the witness
prints NO MAX-single-op line; the flat query line IS the worst-case claim. The build cost is the
honest co-headline (measured OUTSIDE the timed query op, like every member's construction).

## BitSet

    new BitSet(nbits)

- A WORST-CASE O(1) FIXED-capacity multi-word DENSE bitset over MANY Uint32 words (N >> 32) --
  the suite's canonical membership / flag structure for visited sets, dirty masks, replay
  windows, and permission bitmaps at scale. Bits are [0, nbits). It is a MUTABLE worst-case
  member in the mainstream cohort (SparseSet / RandomSet), the fourteenth member.
- nbits: fixed bit-capacity; integer in [1, 2^25] (33,554,432 bits, 4 MiB of data words).
  Constructor throws a [lite-o1] RangeError on a non-integer / < 1 / > 2^25 / NaN nbits
  (Number.isInteger never coerces; String(nbits) message is Symbol / BigInt-safe), thrown BEFORE
  any store is allocated so nothing half-built escapes.
- Substrate (flat SoA, pointer-free): ONE Uint32Array `_w` of ceil(nbits/32) DATA words (bit i
  at _w[i >>> 5], mask 1 << (i & 31)), plus a 3-LEVEL popcount SUMMARY (fan-out 32) `_s1` /
  `_s2` / `_s3` where each summary bit records whether the word below it is non-empty. At the
  2^25 ceiling: W = 2^20 data words, _s1 = 2^15 words, _s2 = 2^10 words, _s3 = 32 words (the
  FIXED top scan). Summary overhead ~ n/1024 words. Every index stays below 2^31 -> SMI-safe,
  no boxing on the hot path.

Hot surface (per-bit test / set / unset / toggle + firstSet / nextSet are all WORST-CASE
O(1), zero allocation):

- test(i) -> boolean     True iff bit i is set. One word load + one mask test, no branch past the
                         guard. A bad index (negative, fractional, NaN, null, Symbol, BigInt, or
                         >= capacity) is ABSENT (false), NEVER a throw and NEVER bit 0 (typeof
                         guard FIRST so a Symbol / BigInt never reaches the coercing >>>).
- set(i) -> this         Set bit i. Fail closed: a bad index throws [lite-o1]. Updates the summary
                         when the affected word transitions empty -> non-empty.
- unset(i) -> this       Unset (clear) bit i -- the per-bit companion to set(i). Fail closed: a bad
                         index throws [lite-o1] (NEVER a silent whole-set wipe -- null is not zero;
                         the whole-set reset is the no-arg clear() below). Updates the summary when
                         the word transitions to empty.
- toggle(i) -> this      Flip bit i. Fail closed on a bad index; updates the summary across the
                         empty<->non-empty boundary.
- firstSet() -> index|-1 The lowest set bit index, or -1 if none. WORST-CASE O(1) via the summary
                         (a fixed <= 32-word top scan + a 3-hop clz32/ctz32 descent, never an
                         O(words) scan). Never throws. -1 is the "no set bits" sentinel.
- nextSet(from) -> index|-1  The lowest set bit index >= from, or -1. WORST-CASE O(1). A bad from
                         (non-number, non-uint32, or >= capacity) returns -1 and NEVER throws.

Bulk + reset surface (O(words) -- a DISCLOSED co-headline, NOT the per-bit claim; each is still
0 B/op, writing into the existing words -- the torture gate proves the allocation claim
separately from the O(words) time claim):

- and(other) / or(other) / xor(other) / andNot(other) -> this  In-place set-algebra between two
                         SAME-capacity BitSets. Fail closed: a non-BitSet or a capacity mismatch
                         throws [lite-o1]. Each REBUILDS the summary (a stale summary after a
                         bulk write would be a silent firstSet corruption).
- popcount() -> number   Number of set bits (a full word scan). `size` getter is an alias.
- setAll() -> this       Set every bit in [0, capacity); bits beyond capacity stay 0. Rebuilds
                         the summary.
- clear() -> this        WHOLE-SET reset (takes NO argument): zero every data + summary word in
                         place (no store is reallocated). Use unset(i) to clear a single bit.
- forEach(fn) -> void    Invoke fn(index, bitset) for every set bit in ASCENDING order,
                         alloc-free. O(popcount) over the summary. A HOISTED callback keeps it
                         allocation-free (the documented scan exception).
- [Symbol.iterator]()    Iterate the set-bit indices ascending; the summary descent allocates
                         nothing, but the generator protocol yields a {value, done} per step --
                         OUT of the zero-alloc claims (use forEach for the alloc-free scan).
- capacity (getter)      Fixed bit-capacity (nbits).
- size (getter)          Number of set bits (popcount; O(words), not O(1)).

NON-OVERLAP (LOCKED, settled by the 2026-09-22 audit): BitSet is the MULTI-WORD, arbitrary-N
structure. @zakkster/lite-fastbit32 stays the SINGLE 32-flag word; @zakkster/lite-scheduler's
FastBitScheduler stays the bit-bucket scheduler; lite-o1's own BucketQueue stays the priority
queue. BitSet reuses fastbit32's branchless word-op idiom by DESIGN-PARITY ONLY -- never a
runtime dependency (the zero-deps law; the SlotPool / NodePool borrow-without-depend precedent).
Membership / flags only -- it never drifts into scheduling.

Worst-case honesty: like SparseSet / RandomSet / RingLog / SparseTable, every per-bit op is
WORST-CASE O(1) (a fixed word load + mask op, never a run), and firstSet / nextSet are
WORST-CASE O(1) via the summary -- so the witness prints NO MAX-single-op line; the flat per-bit
line IS the claim. The O(words) bulk ops are the honest co-headline (like SparseTable's build).

## AliasTable

    new AliasTable(weights, seed = 0x9e3779b1)

- A WORST-CASE O(1) STATIC Vose weighted sampler: build a table from a fixed weight vector ONCE
  (an O(n) precompute), then draw an outcome index in [0, n) by WEIGHT in worst-case O(1). The
  WEIGHTED complement to RandomSet (which draws UNIFORMLY): loot tables, weighted load-balancing,
  Monte-Carlo, procedural generation -- all otherwise hand-roll an O(n) cumulative scan. The
  suite's SECOND static build-once / immutable member, the fifteenth member.
- weights: the outcome weights; a real Array or a numeric TypedArray, length n in [1, 2^26].
  COPIED into an owned Float64Array (the table is immutable -- a later caller mutation can never
  change an already-built table). Every weight must be typeof 'number' AND finite AND >= 0, with
  at least one strictly > 0; a non-array / empty / bad-length weights, or a NaN / +/-Infinity /
  negative / non-numeric element, or an all-zero vector, throws [lite-o1] (typeof guard FIRST so a
  Symbol / BigInt never coerces), thrown BEFORE any table is allocated so nothing half-built escapes.
- seed: optional RNG seed; any integer (coerced to uint32), default 0x9e3779b1, per-instance.
- Substrate (flat SoA, pointer-free): `_prob` (Float64Array(n)) per-column accept probability in
  [0, 1]; `_alias` (Uint32Array(n)) per-column fallback outcome; `_w` (Float64Array(n)) the owned
  copy of the input weights (weightOf reads it). The Vose build partitions the scaled weights into
  small (<1) / large (>=1) worklists over ONE pre-allocated Int32Array scratch (a small stack from
  the front, a large stack from the back -- no per-step allocation); scratch + scaled temporaries
  are discarded build locals, never instance fields. PRNG: a per-instance Numerical-Recipes LCG
  (s = (s*1664525 + 1013904223) >>> 0), DUPLICATED inline (RandomSet's idiom) so there is no shared
  mutable module state and tree-shaking stays intact.

Hot surface (sample is WORST-CASE O(1), zero allocation):

- sample() -> index          Draw an outcome index in [0, n) by weight. WORST-CASE O(1), zero-alloc,
                             NEVER throws for any PRNG state. Two LCG advances: the first word's
                             HIGH bits pick a column (floor(s / 2^32 * n), NOT s % n -- the LCG's
                             low bits are weak), the second word's high bits give a uniform in
                             [0, 1) compared against _prob[col]; below it accept the column, else
                             fall through to its alias. Advances the per-instance RNG word.
- weightOf(i) -> number      The ORIGINAL input weight of outcome i (from the owned copy). O(1).
                             A non-integer / out-of-range i returns 0 and NEVER throws (a
                             zero-weight outcome is never sampled anyway; typeof guard FIRST).
- clear() -> this            Reset the PRNG to the construction seed. O(1). The table is IMMUTABLE
                             (nothing else to reset), so the sample() sequence restarts exactly.
- forEach(fn) -> void        Invoke fn(weight, index, table) over the original weights in outcome
                             order, alloc-free. O(n) -- the documented scan exception. A HOISTED
                             callback keeps it allocation-free.
- size (getter)              Number of outcomes n (sample() returns an index in [0, size)).
- seed (getter)             The RNG seed clear() resets to (uint32).

Build-once, sample-only: there are NO mutators (no reweight / update-weight -- a reweight is an
O(n) rebuild, disclosed as future work) and no [Symbol.iterator]. The only allocator is the
constructor; sample / weightOf / forEach allocate ZERO bytes.

Worst-case honesty: sample() is WORST-CASE O(1) (two LCG advances + one compare + one read,
independent of n and the weight skew), so like SparseTable / BitSet it prints NO MAX-single-op
line -- the flat sample line IS the claim. The O(n) BUILD + 2n Float64/Uint32 SPACE are the honest
co-headline (paid once at construction, EXCLUDED from the per-op claim, the SparseTable precedent).

## WindowFold

A zero-GC, WORST-CASE O(1) GENERAL FIFO sliding-window aggregator (DABA-Lite -- the De-Amortized
Banker's Aggregator, Tangwongsan/Hirzel/Schneider, IBM Research, arXiv:2009.13768) over TWO
Float64Array columns (raw value + partial aggregate) in one power-of-two ring. The seventeenth
member and the GENERAL complement to MonoDeque: where MonoDeque does sliding min/max in AMORTIZED
O(1) via a monotonic deque, WindowFold folds ANY of FOUR frozen associative operators over the live
window in TRUE WORST-CASE O(1).

Operator (frozen at construction, the MonoDeque kind pattern): one of the four names 'SUM' | 'MIN' |
'MAX' | 'PRODUCT', cached as an int that drives a SWITCH-FREE combine (no operator-string test, no
lambda on the hot path). Identities: SUM -> 0, MIN -> +Infinity, MAX -> -Infinity, PRODUCT -> 1 --
returned verbatim by query() on an EMPTY window (null is not zero: an empty SUM window IS 0).

Model (DABA-Lite -- a de-amortized banker's two-stacks): a FRONT region holds SUFFIX aggregates
(so its head is the whole front aggregate) and a BACK region folds into one running accumulator;
query() = combine(front, back). The classic two-stacks would FLIP (reverse the back into a fresh
front when the front empties) with an O(W) evict spike; DABA-Lite DE-AMORTIZES that flip into a
REVERSE phase then a MERGE phase, ONE combine per push/evict, so no single op does more than TWO
combines and there is NO O(W) spike. It therefore prints NO max-single-op line (the worst-case
cohort with MinStack / TimerWheel / SparseTable / BitSet / CoarseTimerWheel).

Constructor: new WindowFold(capacity, op) -- capacity an integer in [1, 2^31], ROUNDED UP to the
next power of two (the RingDeque / MonoDeque ring precedent); op one of the four frozen names.
Fail closed: a bad capacity or a bad op (non-string, unknown name, or an inherited object key like
'constructor') throws [lite-o1] BEFORE any store is allocated.
