- push(v) -> this           O(1) worst-case, 0 B/op. Append v as the newest element (folded into
                            the running back sum) + one de-amortized flip step. typeof guard FIRST
                            (a non-number / NaN throws; +/-Infinity accepted). A FULL ring throws
                            [lite-o1] as a byte-identical no-op; the 2^53 position ceiling throws.
- evict() -> this           O(1) worst-case, 0 B/op. Drop the OLDEST element + one flip step. An
                            EMPTY window is a no-op (never throws).
- query() -> number         O(1) worst-case (<= 2 combines), 0 B/op. The current window aggregate;
                            the operator IDENTITY on an empty window. NEVER throws.
- size (getter)             Number of live elements.
- capacity (getter)         Max simultaneously-live elements (power-of-two, rounded up).
- op (getter)               The frozen operator name ('SUM' | 'MIN' | 'MAX' | 'PRODUCT').
- clear() -> void           O(1): resets positions + running sum + flip state; touches NO store.
- forEach(fn) -> void       O(size) alloc-free scan FRONT -> BACK (oldest -> newest); fn is
                            (value, index, fold).
- [Symbol.iterator]()       O(size) scan, same order; ALLOCATES per protocol -- use forEach.

Caller-driven primitive (the MonoDeque style, not a fixed-width policy): the caller owns which
elements are in the window (count-based, time-based, event-based). Non-overlap: MonoDeque (min/max
only, amortized), MinStack (stack lifetime, no eviction), SparseTable (static build-once), and
@zakkster/lite-logn Fenwick (arbitrary-index mutable range, O(log n)). The bitwise trio (AND / OR /
XOR) is DEFERRED to a future int32-lane sibling WindowFoldInt32 (a Float64 aggregate lane cannot
honestly carry 32-bit bitwise semantics); MINMAX / SUMSQ / COUNT / GCD are dropped (see ADR 0023).

## RankSelect

A zero-GC, WORST-CASE O(1) STATIC succinct rank/select bitvector index over a frozen bit pattern
(cs-poppy -- Zhou/Andersen/Kaminsky, SEA 2013: 512-bit basic blocks + a select sampling layer).
The eighteenth member and the succinct primitive the ecosystem was missing: rank1/select1 are the
substrate of wavelet trees, succinct tries, monotone integer sets, and compressed suffix arrays.
@zakkster/lite-loglogn re-adopts it as its rank/select substrate (never forks). It is the THIRD
static build-once / immutable member (after SparseTable + AliasTable).

Source: a RAW WORD ARRAY (a real Array or a numeric TypedArray, uint32 per element) + an explicit
nbits. The first ceil(nbits/32) words are COPIED (coerced via >>> 0) into a private Uint32Array; bits
at or above nbits are masked to 0. This is NOT a BitSet instance -- zero coupling to the mutable
member (the SparseTable / AliasTable copy-not-reference discipline). Build-once, query-only: NO
mutators (rebuild to change).

Geometry (cs-poppy, ~3.2% index overhead, beating SDSL v5's 6.25%): L0 = absolute Float64
super-block cumulative counts (2^32 bits/super; one super-block covers the <= 2^25-bit range, so L0
is a single 0, present for design parity); L1 = per-lower-block (2048-bit) cumulative popcount
(Uint32); L2 = per-lower-block packed relative counts (three 10-bit basic-block popcounts in one
Uint32); L3 = the per-word popcount prefix computed on the fly by the bounded <= 16-word in-block
scan (NOT a stored array -- that would be ~50% overhead). A select sample is stored every 8192 set
bits (and every 8192 clear bits, for select0).

Constructor: new RankSelect(source, nbits) -- nbits an integer in [1, 2^25]. Fail closed: a bad
nbits (non-integer / 0 / > 2^25 / NaN / null / Symbol) throws [lite-o1] BEFORE any typed array is
allocated (the typeof-safe Number.isInteger guard runs FIRST); then a non-Array / non-TypedArray
source throws.

- rank1(i) -> number        O(1) worst-case, 0 B/op. Set bits in [0, i). Bad i -> 0; i > length
                            clamps to length (rank1(length) === size). NEVER throws.
- rank0(i) -> number        O(1) worst-case, 0 B/op. Clear bits in [0, i) -- free (i - rank1(i)).
- select1(k) -> number      O(1) worst-case, 0 B/op. Position of the k-th set bit (0-indexed) via
                            the sample layer + a bounded in-block scan (NOT rank + binary search).
                            Bad / overflow k (>= size) -> -1. NEVER throws.
- select0(k) -> number      O(1) worst-case, 0 B/op. Position of the k-th clear bit -- free from the
                            same directory (512*b - rank1) + a clear-bit sample layer. Bad k -> -1.
- access(i) -> 0|1|undefined  O(1) worst-case, 0 B/op. The bit at i; undefined for a bad i.
- size (getter)             Number of set bits (popcount, precomputed at build). O(1).
- length (getter)           Number of bits (nbits). O(1).
- indexBytes (getter)       The cs-poppy directory byte footprint (the disclosed ~3.2% overhead). O(1).
- forEach(fn) -> void       O(nbits) alloc-free scan of set-bit indices ASCENDING; fn is (index, rs).
- [Symbol.iterator]()       O(nbits) set-bit-index scan; ALLOCATES per protocol -- use forEach.

Honesty contract (SparseTable ADR 0018 + AliasTable ADR 0020): the hot ops are TRUE worst-case O(1);
the O(n) build + the ~3.2% index space are a DISCLOSED co-headline, EXCLUDED from the per-op claim,
so there is NO max-single-op line (the flat rank line IS the worst-case claim; the witness foil is a
naive O(words) popcount scan). Non-overlap: BitSet (ADR 0019) is the MUTABLE membership / flag
structure with no rank/select; RankSelect is the IMMUTABLE succinct index over a frozen bit pattern.

## EliasFano

    new EliasFano(source)

- source: a SORTED (monotone non-decreasing) sequence of n non-negative integers in [0, U) -- a
  numeric Array or any numeric TypedArray. U is INFERRED as (last value + 1). The values are ENCODED
  into a private store, not referenced (a later mutation of the caller's array never changes the codec).
- Constructor fails closed (typeof-first, BEFORE any typed array is allocated) on a non-array source, a
  non-integer / negative / NaN / BigInt value, a decreasing pair (it does NOT sort internally -- an
  unsorted source is a caller bug), or n / U / the upper bitvector past the ceiling (n <= 2^25).
- Encoding (quasi-succinct, Elias-Fano): L = max(0, floor(log2(U/n))) low bits per value, bit-packed
  into a flat Uint32Array; the upper bits (value >> L) as a unary-gap bitvector indexed by a COMPOSED
  RankSelect (reuse, never a fork). Total ~ n*(2 + L) bits, i.e. ~2 + ceil(log2(U/n)) bits/element --
  near the information-theoretic minimum for a monotone sequence.

Query surface:

- access(i) -> number|undefined  The i-th value (ascending). WORST-CASE O(1): (select1(i) - i)*2^L +
                                 low(i). A bad i is undefined, NEVER throws.
- nextGEQ(x) -> number           The smallest stored value >= x (successor-or-equal). DATA-DEPENDENT:
                                 O(1) TYPICAL on well-distributed keys, O(log n) WORST-CASE on clustered
                                 keys (a select0 bucket seek in O(1) + a bounded in-bucket binary search
                                 over the low bits). Returns -1 when x > max or on a bad x. NEVER throws.
- forEach(fn) -> void            O(n) alloc-free ascending decode; fn is (value, eliasFano).
- [Symbol.iterator]()            O(n) ascending values (ALLOCATES per protocol -- use forEach alloc-free).
- length / size (getter)         The value count n.
- universe (getter)              The inferred exclusive universe U (max + 1; 0 when empty).
- bitsPerElement (getter)        The average encoded bits per element (the succinct co-headline).
- sizeBytes (getter)             The total backing footprint (packed low store + the composed RankSelect).

Honesty contract: access is WORST-CASE O(1) (joins the worst-case cohort, NO max-single-op line); the
O(n) build + the succinct space are DISCLOSED co-headlines paid once (SparseTable ADR 0018 precedent).
nextGEQ is the family's first DATA-DEPENDENT op: O(1) typical / O(log n) worst -- labeled as such, never
sold as a clean expected-O(1) (ADR 0025). Build-once / immutable: NO mutators (rebuild to change).
Non-overlap: RankSelect is the rank/select index over a raw bit pattern; EliasFano is the succinct codec
for a monotone integer SEQUENCE built on it. Sub-logarithmic predecessor/successor (O(log log U)) is
@zakkster/lite-loglogn's domain; arbitrary-index mutable range queries are @zakkster/lite-logn's Fenwick.

## Design bounds

- SparseSet valid key: integer in [0, universe).
- SparseSet fixed capacity: no silent growth; a new key past capacity throws.
- SparseSet fail closed on add, absent on query. null is never coerced to key 0.
- RingDeque fixed capacity (power-of-two, rounded up): push past full throws
  (fail closed); pop/peek on empty returns undefined. Numeric values only.
- RingDeque value: typeof 'number' and not NaN (+/-Infinity accepted).
- UnionFind element: integer in [0, n); fixed n, no growth. Fail closed on a bad
  element (throws [lite-o1]); reset() and forEachRoots() are the O(n) exceptions.
- MonoDeque capacity (power-of-two, rounded up): max simultaneously-live entries;
  push past full throws (fail closed). Value: typeof 'number' and not NaN
  (+/-Infinity accepted). kind frozen at construction. seq ceiling 2^53.
  forEach / [Symbol.iterator] are the O(k) scan exceptions (iterator allocates).
- MinStack capacity (EXACT, NOT rounded): max elements; push past full throws
  (fail closed). Value: typeof 'number' and not NaN (+/-Infinity accepted). kind
  frozen at construction. WORST-CASE O(1) push/pop/peek/extreme. The ext[] column
  doubles memory, so the 2^31 ceiling is a TYPE bound (see the memory note).
  forEach / [Symbol.iterator] scan TOP -> BOTTOM (iterator allocates).
- RandomSet valid key: integer in [0, universe); fixed capacity, no growth. Fail
  closed on add, absent on query (null is never coerced to key 0). seed: any integer
  (coerced to uint32), per-instance. sample() / removeRandom() are WORST-CASE O(1),
  undefined on empty (never throw). High-bits index map (not s % n); residual
  multiply-bias <= n/2^32 disclosed, no rejection sampling. forEach / [Symbol.iterator]
  are the O(size) scan exceptions (iterator allocates).
- FreqO1 valid key: integer in [0, universe); fixed capacity, no growth. Fail closed
  on the mutators add / increment (throws [lite-o1]; null is never coerced to key 0),
  absent on the queries has / frequencyOf (never throw, frequencyOf returns 0). maxFreq
  ceiling in [1, 2^32-2]; an increment past it throws (no wrap). add / increment /
  frequencyOf / has / peekMin / popMin are WORST-CASE O(1); peekMin / popMin undefined
  on empty. FIFO tie-break at equal frequency. Bucket pool sized to capacity + 1 (the
  transient peak), so exhaustion cannot occur; the guard is defense in depth. forEach /
  [Symbol.iterator] scan in dense storage order (iterator allocates). NO decrement, NO
  peekMax, NO delete(k).
- BucketQueue valid key: integer in [0, universe); valid priority: integer in [0, ceiling];
  fixed capacity, no growth. MONOTONE: extractMin drains in non-decreasing priority order,
  the cursor never rewinds; insert / decreaseKey below the cursor throw (fail closed).
  Space O(ceiling). Fail closed on the mutators insert / decreaseKey (throws [lite-o1];
  null is never coerced to key 0), absent on the queries has / priorityOf (never throw;
  priorityOf returns -1). insert / decreaseKey / extractMin / peekMin are AMORTIZED O(1)
  (a single extractMin is O(gap) worst-case); extractMin / peekMin undefined on empty.
  FIFO tie-break within a priority. Static buckets 0..ceiling, no free-list. forEach /
  [Symbol.iterator] scan in dense storage order (iterator allocates). insert of a present
  key, and decreaseKey of an absent key or a non-strict-decrease, are documented no-ops.
- TimerWheel valid id: integer in [0, universe); valid delay: integer in [0, slots-1];
  fixed capacity, no growth. BOUNDED "simple" wheel (Varghese-Lauck): schedule files into
  slot[(now + delay) & MASK]; DRAIN-BEFORE-ADVANCE -- advance() refuses to lap over an
  undrained slot (throws fail-closed), so there is no cursor and no O(gap) worst case.
  Space O(slots). Fail closed on the mutators schedule / advance (throws [lite-o1]; null
  is never coerced to id 0), absent on the queries has / cancel (never throw; cancel
  returns false). schedule / cancel / advance(1) / has are WORST-CASE O(1); drainDue is
  O(due). `now` ceiling 2^53 (a `>=` guard; advance past it throws, no precision loss).
  FIFO within-slot order; drainDue captures next-before-fn (re-entrancy-safe). Static
  slots 0..slots-1, no free-list. forEach / [Symbol.iterator] scan in dense storage order
  (iterator allocates). schedule of a present id is an idempotent no-op (reschedule =
  cancel then schedule). NO pollDue, NO cursor, NO absolute-deadline column.
- HierarchicalTimerWheel valid id: integer in [0, universe); valid delay: integer in
  [0, 2^26); fixed capacity, no growth. CASCADING multi-level wheel (Linux tvec shape
  1x256 + 3x64): schedule files at the level/slot for `delay`; DRAIN-BEFORE-CASCADE --
  advance() refuses to lap over an undrained level-0 slot (throws fail-closed) and cascades
  coarse levels down by INDEX on a wrap. Space O(capacity + 449). Fail closed on the
  mutators schedule / advance (throws [lite-o1]; a delay >= 2^26 throws a byte-identical
  no-op; null is never coerced to id 0), absent on the queries has / cancel (never throw;
  cancel returns false). schedule / cancel / advance(1) / has are AMORTIZED O(1) (a level-
  wrap advance is O(bucket) -- the cascade spike); drainDue is O(due). `now` ceiling 2^53.
  Re-entrant advance throws [lite-o1] (schedule / cancel / clear stay legal in a callback).
  FIFO within-list order. Static 449 lists, no free-list. forEach (id, expiry, wheel) /
  [Symbol.iterator] scan in dense storage order (iterator allocates). schedule of a present
  id is an idempotent no-op. The foil is a FAIR 4-ary min-heap (O(log n)), not a strawman.
- RingLog valid value: typeof 'number' and not NaN (+/-Infinity accepted); fixed capacity
  (power-of-two, rounded up), no growth. LOSSY overwrite-oldest: push NEVER blocks / throws
  on full -- it overwrites the oldest and RETURNS it (undefined until full); fail closed on
  the VALUE only (a non-number / NaN throws [lite-o1] a byte-identical no-op; null never
  coerced). READ-ONLY snapshot surface (get / oldest / newest / forEach / iterate); NO
  popOldest / drain (inverts RingDeque's fail-closed policy -- two honest members, not one).
  push / get / oldest / newest are WORST-CASE O(1); get out-of-range / non-int returns
  undefined, oldest / newest undefined on empty (never throw). forEach / [Symbol.iterator]
  scan oldest -> newest (iterator allocates).
- CuckooMap valid key: any safe integer, |k| <= 2^53 (Number.isSafeInteger); valid value:
  typeof 'number' and not NaN (+/-Infinity accepted). Fixed capacity (rounded up under a 0.90
  load ceiling), no growth. BUCKETIZED cuckoo (2 tables x 4 slots): get / has / delete are
  WORST-CASE O(1) (<= 8 slot reads); set is AMORTIZED O(1) (eviction chain bounded by
  MaxLoop = 8*log2(cap), then one in-place O(capacity) re-seed -- the max-single-op line).
  Fail closed on set (a NEW key past the ceiling / an unplaceable key throws [lite-o1], a
  byte-identical no-op on the load-ceiling reject; a bad key / value throws typeof-first),
  absent / false on the queries get / has / delete (never throw). 0 is a LEGAL key + any finite
  number a legal value -- emptiness is a Uint8Array occupancy byte, never a 0 sentinel; no
  tombstones (a lookup visits only the two home buckets). Space O(capacity) over a sparse /
  large integer key domain (vs SparseSet's O(universe) over a dense one). clear() is O(capacity)
  (a Uint8Array fill). forEach / [Symbol.iterator] scan in dense slot order (iterator allocates).
- SparseTable valid source: a real Array of numbers or a numeric TypedArray, length in [1, 2^26];
  every element typeof 'number' and not NaN (+/-Infinity accepted). STATIC build-once / immutable:
  the source is COPIED into an internal Float64Array (a post-build mutation of the caller's array
  cannot invalidate a query); NO mutators, NO clear. query(l, r) / at(i) are WORST-CASE O(1)
  (query = a floor-log2 via clz32 + two table reads + one compare, the idempotent-overlap trick),
  undefined on a bad l / r / i (never throw). The O(n log n) BUILD + O(n log n) table SPACE
  (n*(floor(log2 n)+1) table cells + n source cells) are a DISCLOSED co-headline paid once at
  construction, EXCLUDED from the per-op claim (like BucketQueue's O(ceiling) / TimerWheel's
  O(slots)). Fail closed at construction (a non-array / empty / bad-length source, a bad kind, or
  a non-numeric / NaN element throws [lite-o1] a byte-identical no-op -- nothing half-built
  escapes), queries never throw. kind ('min' | 'max') frozen. forEach / [Symbol.iterator] scan the
  source values in index order (iterator allocates). NO max-single-op line (query is worst-case
  O(1); the build cost is the honest co-headline, not a per-op spike).
- BitSet valid nbits: integer in [1, 2^25]; bits are [0, nbits). FIXED capacity, no growth. Per-bit
  test / set / unset / toggle are WORST-CASE O(1) (one word load + one mask op past the guard);
  firstSet / nextSet are WORST-CASE O(1) via a 3-level popcount summary (fan-out 32; a fixed
  <= 32-word top scan + a 3-hop clz32/ctz32 descent, never an O(words) scan). Fail closed on the
  MUTATORS (set / unset / toggle throw [lite-o1] on an out-of-range index; null is never
  coerced to bit 0), ABSENT on the QUERIES (test returns false, firstSet / nextSet return -1;
  never throw). Bulk and / or / xor / andNot (in place, same-capacity-or-throw) + popcount / setAll
  / clear() (whole-set reset) are O(words) -- a DISCLOSED co-headline (like SparseTable's build),
  NOT the per-bit claim, and still 0 B/op. unset(i) clears a single bit; clear() takes NO argument
  and resets the whole set (a bad-index unset THROWS, never a silent wipe -- fail closed). -0
  aliases bit 0 via the uint32 coercion. forEach /
  [Symbol.iterator] yield set-bit indices in ascending order (iterator allocates). NO max-single-op
  line (worst-case cohort). NON-OVERLAP: the MULTI-WORD structure vs lite-fastbit32's single 32-flag
  word + lite-scheduler's FastBitScheduler (design-parity only, ZERO runtime dep).
- AliasTable valid weights: a real Array or numeric TypedArray, length n in [1, 2^26]; every weight
  typeof 'number' && finite && >= 0, at least one > 0. STATIC build-once / immutable: the weights
  are COPIED in, there are NO mutators (no reweight -- an O(n) rebuild, disclosed future work) and
  NO [Symbol.iterator]. Fail closed at CONSTRUCTION (a non-array / empty / bad-length weights, a
  NaN / +/-Infinity / negative / non-numeric element, or an all-zero vector throw [lite-o1]
  typeof-first, before any table is allocated). sample() is WORST-CASE O(1) (two LCG advances +
  one compare + one read, independent of n), returns an index in [0, n), NEVER throws; weightOf(i)
  returns the original weight (0 for a bad index), NEVER throws. PRNG per-instance seeded (LCG
  duplicated inline, no module state); clear() resets to the seed for reproducibility. The O(n)
  BUILD + 2n Float64/Uint32 SPACE are the disclosed co-headline (paid once, EXCLUDED from the per-op
  claim). NO max-single-op line (worst-case cohort). forEach is the O(n) alloc-free scan exception.
- CoarseTimerWheel valid id: integer in [0, universe); valid delay: integer in [0, MAX_DELAY)
  where MAX_DELAY = 62 x 2^24 = 0x3E000000 = 1,040,187,392 (~0.97 x 2^30); valid ticks: integer in
  [0, 2^32-1]; fixed capacity, no growth. NON-CASCADING Linux-4.8 coarse-bucket wheel (9 levels x
  64 buckets, shift 3n, gran 8^n): schedule rounds the deadline UP to the finest level whose
  granule-delta is <= 63 and files it there; the timer fires IN PLACE (never cascaded). APPROXIMATE
  fire -- the disclosed co-headline: fire >= now + delay ALWAYS (never early), LATE by at most
  gran(level) - 1 (<= 12.5% relative error, ONE-SIDED; L0 EXACT). DRAIN-BEFORE-ADVANCE -- advance()
  refuses to skip a due bucket (throws fail-closed), validated by the per-bucket occupancy BITMAP
  (18 x Uint32), so advance is WORST-CASE O(1) for ANY k with NO cascade and NO max-single-op line.
  Space O(capacity + 577 + 18). Fail closed on the mutators schedule / advance (throws [lite-o1]; a
  delay >= MAX_DELAY or a NEW id past capacity throws a byte-identical no-op; null never coerced to
  id 0), absent on the queries has / cancel / peekNext / fireTimeOf (never throw; cancel/absent
  false, peekNext/fireTimeOf -1). schedule / cancel / advance(k) are WORST-CASE O(1); drainDue is
  O(due + levels). `now` ceiling 2^53. Re-entrant advance throws [lite-o1] (schedule / cancel /
  clear stay legal in a callback). Finest-first across levels, FIFO within a bucket; drainDue
  SNAPSHOT (a reschedule inside a callback defers). Static 577 buckets, no free-list; the 18-word
  bitmap makes clear() O(1). forEach (id, fireAt, wheel) / [Symbol.iterator] scan in dense storage
  order (iterator allocates). schedule of a present id is an idempotent no-op. NO payload storage;
  for EXACT far-future deadlines use a min-heap (@zakkster/lite-logn). The foil is a FAIR 4-ary
  min-heap (O(log n)), not a strawman.

## Scripts

- npm test           -- 542 node:test cases (contract + boundary + differential fuzz).
- npm run test:types -- tsc --noEmit against O1.d.ts.
- npm run torture    -- lite-leak + lite-gc-profiler: 0 B/op, 0 major GC, leak-free.
- npm run witness    -- O(1) throughput-invariance harness + foils + flatness gate.
- npm run test:perf  -- lite-perf-gate hard zero-alloc scavenge-scaling gate.
- npm run verify     -- all five gates (publish gate).

## Witness gate (locked)

- SparseSet: n-sweep [1e3..1e7] DISPLAYED, batch 1e6, two warm-ups + median of 9.
  The gate is computed over the STEADY window 1e4 <= n <= 1e6: below it (n=1e3) is
  an L1 micro-case that turbo-spikes, above it (n=1e7) is the memory wall where the
  8*n-byte arrays exceed cache and ops/ms measures DRAM, not the algorithm -- both
  are shown but excluded from the gate. SparseSet flatness (opsPerMs last/first over
  the window) >= 0.70; native Set foil flatness <= 0.55 AND SparseSet/Set ops-per-ms
  ratio >= 1.5x at every gated size. (The 0.70 floor is unchanged; only the gate's
  domain is pinned to where ops/ms means O(1).)
- RingDeque: n-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], FIFO churn vs Array.prototype.shift foil
  (O(n)); ops/ms is a rate, so the ring (batch 5e5) and foil (batch 2e3) use
  different batches yet compare directly. RingDeque flatness >= 0.70; shift foil
  flatness <= 0.55; RingDeque/shift ratio >= 1.5x.
- UnionFind: n-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], amortized find (coalesced + flattened) vs a
  NAIVE disjoint-set foil (no path compression, no union-by-size -> a degenerate
  chain, O(n) find). ops/ms is a rate (uf batch 5e5, naive batch 2e3). UnionFind
  flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55; UnionFind/naive ratio >= 1.5x.
- MonoDeque: W-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5] (W is the sliding-window width), amortized
  push + slide vs a NAIVE window-min that RESCANS the whole window each step
  (O(W)/element). ops/ms is a rate (mono batch 5e5, naive batch 300). MonoDeque
  flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55; MonoDeque/naive ratio >= 1.5x.
  The witness also prints the MAX single-op time (an O(W) pop-storm) beside a
  typical O(1) push -- the amortized-honesty bar.
- MinStack: depth-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], WORST-CASE-O(1) extreme() on a strictly-
  DECREASING feed (every push rewrites ext) vs a NAIVE plain-array stack that
  RESCANS all live elements each query (O(depth)). ops/ms is a rate (mstk batch
  5e5, naive batch 300). Gated over the steady window depth >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point
  is a pure-L1 micro-case shown but not gated; the 0.70 floor is unchanged, only
  the domain is pinned). MinStack flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55;
  MinStack/naive ratio >= 1.5x. NO MAX-single-op line: push is worst-case O(1), so
  there is no amortized spike to expose.
- RandomSet: size-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], WORST-CASE-O(1) sample() vs a NAIVE native
  Set that iterates-to-the-k-th element to pick uniformly (O(n)/pick, walked with
  Set.forEach so it allocates nothing per step -- an honest SPEED foil, NOT
  Array.from(set)[k]). ops/ms is a rate (rand batch 5e5, naive batch 300). Gated over
  the steady window size >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a pure-L1 micro-case shown but not
  gated; the 0.70 floor is unchanged, only the domain is pinned). RandomSet flatness
  >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55; RandomSet/naive ratio >= 1.5x. NO
  MAX-single-op line: sample/removeRandom are worst-case O(1) (no rejection loop).
- FreqO1: size-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], WORST-CASE-O(1) increment + peekMin vs a NAIVE
  frequency table (a plain Uint32Array of per-key counts) that LINEARLY SCANS all n
  counts each step to find the LFU key (O(n)/query). ops/ms is a rate (freq batch 5e5,
  naive batch 300). Gated over the steady window size >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a
  pure-L1 micro-case shown but not gated; the 0.70 floor is unchanged, only the domain
  is pinned). FreqO1 flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55; FreqO1/naive ratio
  >= 1.5x. NO MAX-single-op line: add / increment / peekMin / popMin are worst-case
  O(1) (a fixed number of pointer writes, no run).
- BucketQueue: size-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], AMORTIZED-O(1) extractMin (a steady-state
  monotone churn: extractMin + re-insert one bounded window ahead of the cursor) vs an
  ALLOC-FREE binary MIN-HEAP driven by the SAME trace (O(log n) sift per op). ops/ms is a
  rate (both batch 5e5). Gated over the steady window size >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a
  pure-L1 micro-case shown but not gated). BucketQueue flatness >= 0.70; BucketQueue/heap
  ratio >= 1.5x; the heap foil flatness is REPORTED and asserted merely to be LESS flat
  than the bucket queue -- an O(log n) foil decays only ~log(n_lo)/log(n_hi) per decade
  (~0.8) and CANNOT reach the O(n) foils' 0.55 collapse over a steady window, so the
  evidence is the sustained throughput lead, not a foil collapse (see ADR 0013). The
  witness ALSO prints the MAX single-op time (an O(gap) cursor jump across empty buckets)
  beside a typical O(1) extractMin -- the amortized-honesty bar (reported, NOT gated).
- TimerWheel: size-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], WORST-CASE-O(1) TICK (a steady-state
  drainDue + advance, with slots >= n so ~1 timer is due per tick) vs a NAIVE-SCAN
  scheduler that SCANS ALL n pending deadlines each tick to find + fire the due ones
  (O(n)/tick). ops/ms is a rate (wheel batch 5e5, naive batch 2e3). Gated over the steady
  window size >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a pure-L1 micro-case shown but not gated).
  TimerWheel flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55 (a TRUE O(n) foil, so it
  collapses -- unlike BucketQueue's O(log n) heap); TimerWheel/naive ratio >= 1.5x. NO
  MAX-single-op line: schedule / cancel / advance(1) are worst-case O(1) (drain-before-
  advance keeps a slot to one rotation's timers), so there is no amortized spike.
- HierarchicalTimerWheel: size-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], AMORTIZED-O(1) cascading TICK (a
  steady-state drainDue + advance, with the delay horizon scaled to n so ~1 timer is due
  per tick and drained timers re-arm one level up + cascade back down) vs an ALLOC-FREE
  4-ary MIN-HEAP driven by the SAME tick trace (O(log n) per fired timer). ops/ms is a rate
  (both batch 5e5). Gated over the steady window size >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a pure-L1
  micro-case shown but not gated). HierarchicalTimerWheel flatness >= 0.70; HierWheel/heap
  ratio >= 1.5x; the 4-ary heap foil flatness is REPORTED and asserted merely to be LESS
  flat than the wheel -- an O(log n) foil decays gently and CANNOT reach the O(n) foils'
  0.55 collapse, so the evidence is the sustained throughput lead (see ADR 0015 + 0013).
  UNLIKE TimerWheel, it WEARS a MAX-single-op line: the witness gates a visible cascade
  SPIKE (a level-0 wrap re-filing a heavily-loaded level-1 bucket down) at >= 8x the
  typical tick -- the amortized-honesty bar for the cascade, the member's headline.
- CuckooMap: size-sweep [1e4, 1e5, 1e6], bounded-probe WORST-CASE-O(1) lookup (get over a
  mix of hits + misses, <= 8 slot reads) vs a naive O(n) LINEAR-SCAN map (parallel
  Float64Array key/value columns searched by a linear scan, the obvious no-hashing way).
  ops/ms is a rate (map batch 5e5, naive batch 2e2). Gated over the DRAM-resident steady
  window size >= 1e5 (the 1e4 point is an L2 turbo micro-case shown but not gated). CuckooMap
  flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55 (a TRUE O(n) foil, so it collapses);
  CuckooMap/naive ratio >= 1.5x. LIKE HierarchicalTimerWheel it WEARS a MAX-single-op line:
  the witness prints the in-place O(capacity) RE-SEED spike (9 fully-colliding keys trip
  MaxLoop) beside a typical O(1) set, gated as a visible >= 2x spike -- the amortized-honesty
  bar for set.
- SparseTable: len-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], WORST-CASE-O(1) STATIC range-min QUERY over a WIDE range
  (width ~ len; the O(n log n) BUILD is done OUTSIDE the timed op, EXCLUDED from the per-op claim)
  vs an alloc-free O(len) naive range-scan foil (recompute the extreme by scanning [l, len-1] each
  query). Gating over WIDE ranges is deliberate: a narrow range makes the O(len) foil cheap and
  hides the divergence. ops/ms is a rate (table batch 5e5, foil batch 2e3). Gated over the steady
  window len >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a pure-L1 micro-case shown but not gated). SparseTable
  flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55 (a TRUE O(len) foil, so it collapses);
  SparseTable/naive ratio >= 1.5x. NO MAX-single-op line: query is worst-case O(1) (the build cost
  is the honest co-headline, not a per-op spike).
- BitSet: size-sweep [1e4, 1e5, 1e6] (bit capacities), WORST-CASE-O(1) test (a walking membership
  probe over [0, n)) vs a native Set<number> holding the same members (Set.has degrades as its hash
  table + boxed keys outgrow the caches). ops/ms is a RATE (bitset batch 5e5, Set batch 5e5). Gated
  over the DRAM-resident steady window size >= 1e5 (the 1e4 point is an L2 turbo micro-case shown but
  not gated). BitSet flatness >= 0.70; BitSet/Set ratio >= 1.5x. The Set foil DEGRADES gently
  (cache + boxing, NOT asymptotics), so its flatness is REPORTED and asserted merely to be LESS flat
  than BitSet -- it does NOT collapse to the O(n) foils' 0.55 bar (per ADR 0019 + ADR 0013), so the
  evidence is the sustained throughput lead. A SECOND gate is the firstSet O(1) CONTROL: a BitSet
  with a SINGLE bit set at the TOP of an n-bit capacity, timing firstSet() -- worst-case O(1) via
  the summary, so its flatness holds >= 0.70; a scanning firstSet would be O(words) and MISS the
  floor (the T9 fail-path). NO MAX-single-op line: BitSet is worst-case cohort (the O(words) bulk
  ops are the honest co-headline, not a per-op spike).
- CoarseTimerWheel: size-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], WORST-CASE-O(1) NON-CASCADING TICK (a steady-state
  drainDue + advance, with the delay horizon scaled to n so ~1 timer is due per tick and drained
  timers re-arm far ahead into a coarse level, firing IN PLACE) vs an ALLOC-FREE 4-ary MIN-HEAP
  driven by the SAME tick trace (O(log n) per fired timer -- the same fair foil
  HierarchicalTimerWheel uses). ops/ms is a rate (both batch 5e5). Gated over the steady window
  size >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a pure-L1 micro-case shown but not gated). CoarseTimerWheel flatness
  >= 0.70; CoarseWheel/heap ratio >= 1.5x; the 4-ary heap foil flatness is REPORTED and asserted
  merely to be LESS flat than the wheel (an O(log n) foil decays gently, per ADR 0022 + 0013). NO
  MAX-single-op line: schedule / cancel / advance(k) are WORST-CASE O(1) with NO cascade (a
  bitmap-validated advance touches <= 9 levels), so there is no amortized spike -- UNLIKE
  HierarchicalTimerWheel. A scanning-drain control (no bitmap) MISSES the flatness floor (fail-path).
- RankSelect: nbits-sweep [1e3, 1e4, 1e5], WORST-CASE-O(1) STATIC rank1 QUERY (a fixed cs-poppy
  directory lookup + a bounded <= 16-word in-block popcount scan, INDEPENDENT of nbits) vs a naive
  O(words) popcount-scan foil (recompute rank by scanning every word before i). ops/ms is a rate
  (query batch 5e5, foil batch 2e3). Gated over the steady window nbits >= 1e4 (the 1e3 point is a
  pure-L1 micro-case shown but not gated). RankSelect flatness >= 0.70; naive foil flatness <= 0.55
  (a TRUE O(words) foil, so it collapses -- like SparseTable's scan foil); RankSelect/naive ratio
  >= 1.5x. NO MAX-single-op line: rank / select / access are WORST-CASE O(1), and the O(n) build +
  the ~3.2% index space are the disclosed co-headline, not a per-op spike (the SparseTable precedent).

## Not yet shipped

The public API grows one member per release. 1.8.0 adds RankSelect (the eighteenth member; 1.7.0
added WindowFold, 1.6.0 added CoarseTimerWheel, 1.5.0 added AliasTable, 1.4.0 added BitSet, 1.3.0
added SparseTable, 1.2.0 added CuckooMap, 1.1.0 added RingLog). The long-standing "fully unbounded / hashed timer wheel" roadmap item is now
ANSWERED: CoarseTimerWheel is the honest near-unbounded wheel (approximate-fire, worst-case O(1),
no cascade), and for EXACT far-future deadlines the right tool is a min-heap (@zakkster/lite-logn);
the classic hashed-with-rounds wheel is REJECTED (expected-O(1) / worst-case-O(n), ADR 0022).
SlotPool (a free-list slot allocator with generational handles) is CLOSED (ADR 0021).
SparseSet holds membership, not payloads (store values in a parallel SoA
column or @zakkster/lite-arena); RingDeque holds numbers only; UnionFind holds
disjoint-set connectivity over [0, n), not payloads; MonoDeque holds numeric
window extremes only, MinStack holds numeric stack values + their running
extreme only, RandomSet holds integer membership + uniform sampling over
[0, universe), FreqO1 holds integer keys + their access FREQUENCY over
[0, universe) -- an LFU primitive, not a full cache -- and BucketQueue holds integer
keys + their integer PRIORITY over [0, universe) x [0, ceiling] -- a monotone priority
queue, not a general heap (queue integer handles for object payloads) -- TimerWheel
holds integer timer IDS over [0, universe) filed against a delay in [0, slots-1] -- a
BOUNDED simple wheel, one rotation deep -- HierarchicalTimerWheel holds integer timer
IDS over [0, universe) filed against a delay in [0, 2^26) -- a BOUNDED CASCADING four-level
wheel; and CoarseTimerWheel holds integer timer IDS over [0, universe) filed against a delay in
[0, 62 x 2^24) -- a NON-CASCADING near-unbounded wheel with an APPROXIMATE (bounded, one-sided-
late) fire time, NOT an exact one (for EXACT far-future deadlines reach for a min-heap in
@zakkster/lite-logn; all three wheels schedule integer handles for object payloads, not payloads
directly); WindowFold holds numbers only, a FIFO sliding-window aggregate over ONE frozen monoid
(SUM / MIN / MAX / PRODUCT) -- a caller-driven push/evict/query primitive, NOT a keyed store (for
arbitrary-index / out-of-order range queries reach for @zakkster/lite-logn Fenwick; the bitwise
AND/OR/XOR variant is a future int32-lane WindowFoldInt32); and RingLog holds numbers only, a LOSSY
rolling window you READ (keep the last N, overwrite-oldest) -- NOT a consumable queue (reach for
RingDeque to drain / fail closed) --
CuckooMap holds an exact integer-key -> number MAP over sparse / large safe-integer keys
(|k| <= 2^53), O(capacity) space (NOT SparseSet's O(universe) dense set, NOT lite-filter's
approximate membership; map object payloads to integer handles); and SparseTable holds a STATIC
build-once immutable COPY of a numeric source for O(1) range-min / range-max QUERIES only -- NOT a
mutable structure (there are no mutators / no clear; rebuild a new instance to change the data),
NOT a full segment tree (it answers only an idempotent extreme, not sums / updates).
